386YE Summer Solstice Conclave sessions.d: On Friday the Sevenfold Path and Rod and Shield sent Hammers of the Brilliant Shore and Stalwart Stand on Solid Ground to the Sumaah ambassador. Areloe Larmallevés, Vanja and Amalia da Regario took titles, and Ibis Briarheart kept the Archmage of Spring post. Winter declared amity for Tharim. On Saturday the Golden Pyramid was asked to keep exploring Mareave and the Sevenfold Path was sent to Asavea. The Circle of Zulgan Tash was reconciled, and Judgement of the Magisters and Netweaver's Eye entered Imperial lore. Lashonar was moved to neutrality, and the casting of Raise the Rivers against the Madruga blight was endorsed. Edmundo kept the Archmage of Autumn post. A 100-mana college endowment failed.

n.Grendel: The Conclave asked the Golden Pyramid to continue exploring Grendel-held Mareave for another year, at a cost of 20 crystal mana to the Conclave.
n.The Brass Coast: The Conclave endorsed the Freeborn casting of the arcane projection Raise the Rivers, which aims to make the River Scorrero burst its banks and wash the blight from Madruga.
n.Urizen: The Conclave recognised Illyses as the new War Mage, a title now appointed as an Urizen national position, and said it looked forward to continuing the relationship.

t.Madruga: An endorsed Spring ritual, Raise the Rivers, was to flood the River Scorrero so that it would cleanse the blight from the region.
t.Mareave: The Golden Pyramid was asked to carry on exploring Mareave for the next year, following the Digging for fire wind of fortune.

386YE Summer Solstice Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for Bastion, Hahnmark, Karov, Mareave, Miaren, Mitwold, Redoubt, Sarvos, Sermersuaq, Spiral and Weirwater. The Senate appointed Jarrigk Orzel as Imperial Consul and Bernard Dugdale as Imperial Spymaster, alongside many generals and other officers. The Throne named Alaina Ferelith Meliora as Queen's Rose. The Synod chose Tulva as Cardinal of Courage and Silas of the Cenotaph as Cardinal of Wisdom. The Military Council appointed Maggie Potts as Imperial Huntsmarshall, with new Strategoi for the League and the Marches. Bourse seats such as Hakima of Salt and Sand were filled by auction and vote, and candidates declared for several archmage posts.

n.Dawn: Dawn's territory of Weirwater sent Ser Lucan Mortére to the Senate.
n.Grendel: Grendel's territory of Mareave elected Gaddak as its senator.
n.Highguard: Highguard's territory of Bastion returned Asael as its senator.
n.Navarr: Navarr's territory of Miaren elected Llewellyn Leafstalker to the Senate.
n.The League: The League elected senators for Sarvos and Spiral, and the Military Council named Gabrieli di Tassato as Strategos of the League.
n.The Marches: The Marches sent Hal Talbot to the Senate for Mitwold, and the Military Council named Aliss Thorn as Strategos of the Marches.
n.Urizen: Urizen's territory of Redoubt elected Thalia of Netherwatch as its senator.
n.Varushka: Varushka's territory of Karov returned Anatoly Vassian Tatishchev to the Senate.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark elected two senators: Ruana Markling for Hahnmark and Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer for Sermersuaq.

t.Bastion: Asael was elected Senator for Bastion.
t.Hahnmark: Ruana Markling was elected Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Karov: Anatoly Vassian Tatishchev was elected Senator for Karov.
t.Mareave: Gaddak was elected Senator for Mareave.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker was elected Senator for Miaren.
t.Mitwold: Hal Talbot was elected Senator for Mitwold.
t.Redoubt: Thalia of Netherwatch was elected Senator for Redoubt.
t.Sarvos: Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos was elected Senator for Sarvos.
t.Sermersuaq: Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer was elected Senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian was elected Senator for Spiral.
t.Weirwater: Ser Lucan Mortére was elected Senator for Weirwater.

386YE Summer Solstice Senate sessions.d: The Senate renounced claims to the Silver Peaks, Miechernya, Krevsaty, Crows Ridge, Bonewood and Webwood. It ratified a Skouran treaty recognising the conquest of Mareave and granted the Iron Confederacy free trade. It made the Fundindelve mithril mine a Bourse resource and requested appraisals on Mareave and on peace with the Jotun. The Synod may veto a ban on preaching the Way in Asavea. The Guerdon was raised to 250 thrones. Commissions included the City of Dreams, Drycastle's rebuilding, Journeymage Towers, Reed's Roost, Gildenheim's fortification, a smugglers cove in Ayereed and the Capodomus repairs. Two commissions exceeded the limit and were not enacted. The Throne drew 100 thrones for the Dawnish army.

n.Dawn: The Barrens' commission to rebuild Drycastle in Dawnguard was enacted, and the Throne withdrew 100 thrones for the continued construction of the Dawnish army. The restoration of the Castle of Thorns throne room, funded by the Houses of Dawn, passed but was not enacted.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Drycastle lay in ashes and rubble left by the Druj, and the Druj had sacked the Storm Vault in Zenith, which was now repaired.
n.Grendel: The Skouran treaty celebrated the Grendel's defeat in Mareave, and the new Imperial Spymaster announced a smugglers cove in Grendel-held Ayereed to challenge their grip on the Bay of Catazar.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Skouran treaty welcomed the Imperial Orcs as stewards of Mareave. Skarsind saw its Fundindelve mine made a Bourse resource and Gildenheim fortified.
n.Jotun: The Senate commissioned an appraisal from Naomi of Virtue's Rest on making a peace treaty more appealing to the Jotun, citing the honours they had given Imperial generals.
n.Navarr: Miaren's self-funded commission of the Seren City of Dreams passed, but Hercynia's request to appraise the vale as an armoury for Navarr's war against the vallorn failed.
n.The League: The League gained a new Mistress of Ceremonies title, the Capodomus Cathedral repairs in Sarvos and the Vicente School and Orphanage in Spiral. Its Senators also brokered the Iron Confederacy treaty.
n.The Marches: Marcher Bregasland gained two commissions: the Reed's Roost mana sinecure, with a Roost's Reeve, and a Bounders Hall in Ottery, creating the title Bailiff of the Fens.
n.Thule: The Empire renounced forever any claim to the Silver Peaks, Miechernya, Krevsaty, Crows Ridge, Bonewood and Webwood, recognising them as part of Otkodov.
n.Urizen: The Crystal Architect of the Spires became an Imperial title able to build sinecures anywhere, and the Storm Vault in Zenith was rebuilt. Redoubt's motion created the Astral Arcanist.
n.Varushka: The Master of the Koboldi announced the Great Hall of Fabric Arts in Delev, Karov. Volodmartz proposed the renunciation of claims to the Thule lands, and Varushkan senators backed new mystical titles.

t.Ayereed: Imperial Spymaster Bernard Dugdale announced a smugglers cove in this Grendel-held territory, declaring the Empire would wrest the Bay of Catazar from the Grendel.
t.Bregasland: Two commissions went ahead here: the Reed's Roost mana sinecure and a Bounders Hall in Ottery. The territory's senator also seconded the change to Virtue Inquisitors' powers.
t.Mareave: An appraisal on removing the uncooperative quality from Mareave's three regions was commissioned. The Skouran treaty renounced all Skouran claim to the territory and acknowledged its conquest by the Empire.
t.Ossium: The Empire renounced its claim to Bonewood and Webwood. A Journeymage Tower was raised at Bittershore and a statue to Ossium's liberation was built in Galath Fields.
t.Skarsind: The Fundindelve mithril mine was made an Imperial Bourse resource, to be auctioned at the Autumn Equinox, and Gildenheim was fortified.
t.Spiral: The Vicente School and Orphanage was built in Apulus. The restoration of the Castle of Thorns throne room passed but was not enacted.
t.The Barrens: Drycastle in Dawnguard was rebuilt with 50 thrones. The commission also created the titles Knight of Dawnguard and Reeve of Drycastle.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The self-funded Reed's Roost was built here, a sinecure producing mana crystals with a Roost's Reeve appointed by Marcher senators.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: A Journeymage Tower was built here as part of a series meant to remove the threat Dho'uala posed to shipping.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Senate recognised Bonewood as part of Otkodov now and forever and renounced any Imperial claim to it.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: A statue commemorating the liberation of Ossium and the coming of the Way was built at Lomaa, funded by prosperous Ossian citizens.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Senate recognised Webwood as part of Otkodov now and forever and renounced any Imperial claim to it.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: The Legion Engineer fortified Gildenheim with a rank one fortification and runic wards offered by the Tamazi.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Vicente School and Orphanage was built here, a mana ministry training orphans as reckoners and traders under a League-appointed Custodian.

386YE Summer Solstice Synod judgements.d: Corey Wayfarer's mandate, which required a greater majority, committed Navarr to fighting the vallorn, and many assemblies pledged support. Mandates sent missionaries and support to Asavea and fleets to aid the Sumaah. They also consecrated the Spires of Dusk to Ambition, sent Urizen magicians to bring in the Marcher harvest, and removed the Black Plateau's penalties in Spiral. Statements warned of the Druj along the eastern border and addressed Mareave, the Rahvin and the paragon Vardas, now found never to have existed. Bohemond de Rondell lost his Astolat seat and Hugh Farrier was removed as Champion of Prosperity. Amika Acciai and Dogri Thulebane were recognised as exemplars. Sabella of the Silent Tide sought a veto of the Senate's ban on preaching in Asavea.

n.Dawn: Dawn lost Bohemond de Rondell as Senator for Astolat, and its assembly rejected a call to settle the Barrens but declared the territory Dawnish forever. The assembly also backed the Rahvin claim to the Fangs and urged Dawn to strike the Druj before turning on the vallorn.
n.Druj: The Synod warned that the Druj were active in Therunin, the Barrens and Morrow. Highborn statements called for their removal from the continent and for Highguard to rebuild the Salt Flats of Sanath afterwards.
n.Grendel: The Wisdom assembly urged veterans to teach the Empire how to kill Grendel sharks and kraken. Other statements called on fleets to train against the kraken the Grendel had loosed, and the Tamazi were sent to Mareave partly to guard it against the Grendel threat.
n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly invited Navarr Guides and Wintermark Stormcrows to teach at Bastion and declared peerless kinship with Navarr in Therunin. It also claimed a destiny to rebuild the Salt Flats of Sanath and sent the unconquered into Southmoor to spoil Jotun caches.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Freeborn and Pride assemblies recognised the nation's chosen name, the Unshackled. Marcher and Freeborn farmers were urged to help cultivate arid Mareave, and an enacted mandate sent the Tamazi there. The Imperial Orc assembly also invited the Rahvin back to help them survive the coming winter.
n.Jotun: Navarr called on its people to prepare to reclaim Liathaven from the Jotun. The Marcher miners of the Mournwold were urged to fight the Jotun invasion, and an enacted mandate set Highborn unconquered to spoiling Jotun supply caches in Southmoor.
n.Navarr: A greater-majority mandate committed Navarr to fighting the vallorn, and nations from Dawn to the League pledged their support. Navarr also swore kinship with the Great Forest Orcs and called for Rhonwen's Fall to be rebuilt.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly sent farmers to help make Mareave fertile and warned those along the Scorrero of flooding from the plan to cleanse the Great Grasses. It also urged captains to explore the east, proposed rebuilding Siroc's orphanage alongside the Sumaah, and castigated Ramos for marching on the dhomiro's meeting.
n.The League: League judgements addressed the rat plague in Temeschwar, the Tassato orphans' rivalry with Sanvar Isk and fair wages for Urizeni workers in Spiral. An enacted mandate urged Apulian to welcome Urizen magicians, and another launched a hunt for cannibal butchers in Holberg.
n.The Marches: A Urizen mandate sent magicians to help bring in the Marcher harvest. A Marcher mandate will add the smith archetype after the Autumn Equinox, and beaters were sent after the traitor Dalton Royse. Marchers were also warned of an Asavean attack on Meade.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the recognition of Dogri Thulebane as an exemplar noted that the Thule took Crow's Ridge after his stand.
n.Urizen: Urizen backed its Skyways project, a higher Arch of the Sky and the new national warmage position. Its magicians were sent to help with the Marcher harvest and to use the mithril block in Spiral again. Urizen fleets were not moved by the general mandate to aid the Sumaah.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan assembly urged the Iron Helms to master curses and warned of wolves crossing the warded roads. It also declared Delev open for trade and honoured the wardens whose deeds had been credited to the fictional Vardas. Separately, the Nine set the Silent Bell to investigate the Warhound Assembly in Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Stormcrows were invited to teach at Bastion, Kindra Surefoot entered the Book of Heroes and Dogri Thulebane was recognised as an exemplar of Loyalty. The Wintermark assembly also denounced Siakha's boons, urged hospitality to the mystics of Ishal and revived talk of Gunnar's Deephall.

t.Astolat: Bohemond de Rondell was revoked and removed as Senator for Astolat over his pursuit of the Barrens for Dawn alone.
t.Bastion: Highborn judgements invited Navarr and Wintermark delegations to teach in Bastion once the Grand Inspiration of the Way is complete. A Freeborn mandate to rally support for the holy city failed.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: one judgement wrongly placed the great cathedral in Casinea, when the Grand Inspiration is being built in Bastion.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: notes record Great Forest Orc steadings around weirwood groves in Hercynia.
t.Holberg: An enacted League mandate sent hunters to root out a conspiracy of cannibal butchers beneath Holberg. The Sand Fishers living in Holberg were invited to Anvil.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Dogri Thulebane's recognition cited the opportunity to build his tomb in the Sovevann in Kallavesa.
t.Karsk: The Council of Nine directed the Silent Bell to investigate the funding of the Warhound Assembly in Karsk. Varushka also recalled Navarr standing with it when Karsk was attacked.
t.Liathaven: The Navarr assembly called on the few remaining steadings, and any willing stridings, to prepare provisions and weapons for thorns marching to reclaim Liathaven from the Jotun.
t.Madruga: An Ambition statement cited the kraken the Children of Wrecks had loosed in Madruga's waters and called on Marcher and Wintermark fleets to train to face them.
t.Mareave: The League welcomed Mareave's assignment to the Imperial Orcs and encouraged trade through Spiral. Marcher and Freeborn farmers were urged to help cultivate its arid land, and an enacted mandate sent the Tamazi there.
t.Miaren: Navarr called for Rhonwen's Fall to be rebuilt after the Cold Sun's scions desecrated it. Highborn who defended Miaren with the Granite Pillar were given Loyal Pilgrim testimonies.
t.Mitwold: The Marcher assembly warned that Asavean forces sought to sack Meade and promised that the Drakes were coming home. Mitwold's new senator, Hal Talbot, was called to inquisition.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold miners were urged to rise against the Jotun invaders, and unconquered were sent to spoil Jotun caches in Southmoor. The Pride assembly also called artisans to build the Orchard of the Watch memorial in the ruins of Overton.
t.Ossium: The Synod warned that the Druj threaten the eastern border from Ossium to Zenith. Vasili, the Pride of Ossium, was called to inquisition over his past life vision.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Highborn assembly declared that once the Druj are defeated, Highguard should govern the Salt Flats of Sanath and rebuild Leen as a beacon of the Way.
t.Spiral: An enacted Urizen mandate removed the Black Plateau's penalties on Spiral's economy through use of the mithril block. Urizeni were urged to explore its vacant spires, and the League warned that Black Plateau tours were a scam.
t.Tassato: The League assembly challenged the orphans of Tassato to pitch a plan to rival Sanvar Isk's college, promising its support.
t.Temeschwar: The League assembly urged vigilance against the rat plague in Temeschwar, and its bishops opened their doors to the sick.
t.The Barrens: An enacted mandate consecrated the Spires of Dusk to Ambition. A Dawnish call to settle the Barrens failed, but the Dawnish assembly declared the territory Dawnish forever and pledged to defend its foreign peoples too. 'Race for the Barrens' was put forward as the winning song in the Weavers of Culwich's contest, though it fell short of the greater majority needed.
t.Therunin: With the Druj invading Therunin, Highguard pledged support under peerless kinship and Navarr guarded against hatred. Navarr also warned that Agramant preys on the desperate in the territory now outside the Empire.
t.Zenith: Urizen recognised the plan to raise a higher Arch of the Sky for Zenith's prosperity, while the Synod warned that the Druj threaten the border reaching to Zenith.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: Mentioned in passing: a failed recognition of Doctor Tolame cited the ministry hospital he founded in Sybella Cross.
r.Casinea/Woodwych: Mentioned in passing: Ardeniel of Woodwych Harts was among the Highborn given Loyal Pilgrim testimonies by Navarr.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Prosperity and League assemblies invited the Sand Fishers of Misericorde to a cultural exchange at Anvil, praising their work on the Flaxen Pillars weirwood grove.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The waters around Free Landing, infested with immature kraken in Spring, prompted an Ambition call for fleets to train to slay them.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Marcher assembly called on the miners of the Mourn to arm and come down the hillside against the Jotun, recalling the Ore Hills rebellion.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: An enacted Highborn mandate sent vigilant unconquered to root out and spoil the Jotun's hidden supply caches in Southmoor.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish judgement noted the Emperor vetoed the Rahvin treaty because it would have given away Dawnish homes in Bitter Strand.

386YE Summer Solstice event schedule.d: Nine nations held senatorial elections in their camps on Saturday afternoon, each by its own custom. Tally of the Votes elections for national titles followed from 3:30pm. The Senate sat on Friday night, Saturday afternoon and evening, and Sunday afternoon, with deadlines for motions before each session. The Military Council met after the Saturday and Sunday battles off Anvil. Conclave convened on Friday and Saturday evenings, and the Saturday events included Grandmaster elections and the auction for Imperial Bourse positions. The Synod was open for judgements throughout. Citizen-organised meetings appeared alongside official ones, including a Friday meeting on the Thule, the Vallorn Guard meeting and a Senate Motions dance.

n.Dawn: Dawn elected the senator for Weirwater at 2:30pm on Saturday in its camp, immediately after the tourney.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Mareave, which it held, appears in the schedule's senatorial election listings under the Imperial Orcs.
n.Highguard: Highguard began its inquisition of candidates for the Bastion senatorship at 2:00pm. It elected the Vigilant Swan, the Cinderpath Custodian and the Golden Fleet Salvagemaster by Tally of the Votes at 5:00pm in the Chapel.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were listed to hold a senatorial election for Mareave at 2:15pm, with candidates presenting items of worth. They elected the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting at the Fire Pit at 4:30pm.
n.Navarr: Navarr elected the Miaren senator at 1:30pm, immediately after standing. It chose the Broker of Treji Wayhouse at the Standing Circle at 5:00pm.
n.The League: The League elected senators for both Sarvos and Spiral at 2:30pm through the presentation of collected bonds. It chose the Northbound Trademaster, the Keeper of the Tome and the Master of Rings at the Plaza at 5:30pm.
n.The Marches: The landowners of the Marches gathered at 1:30pm to elect the Mitwold senator. The Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange and the Master of the Root and Stem were chosen at the Community Hall at 3:30pm.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a citizen-organised Friday-evening meeting about the Thule was booked in the Hall of Worlds.
n.Urizen: Urizen's demos for the Redoubt senatorship began at 2:00pm. The Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks, the Architect of the Crucible and the Architect of the Conscious River were elected near the Net of Heaven at 4:00pm.
n.Varushka: Varushka began questioning candidates for the Karov senatorship at 1:45pm. It elected the Granites of Veltsgorsk, the Boyar of the Iron Roads, the Burgher of Ketsov and the Custodian of the Shchaslyvyy Spile at the Central Hearth at 5:30pm.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark elected senators for Sermersuaq and Hahnmark at 2:00pm, with the jars placed down for 30 minutes. It chose the Kalpaheim Tradeholder at the Tree of Names at 3:30pm.

t.Bastion: Bastion's senator was elected by Highguard, beginning with the inquisition of candidates at 2:00pm on Saturday.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator was elected by Wintermark at 2:00pm, although the next regular election for the seat was due at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.
t.Karov: Karov's senator was chosen by Varushka, with questioning of candidates beginning at 1:45pm.
t.Mareave: A senatorial election for Mareave was listed under the Imperial Orcs at 2:15pm, with candidates presenting items of worth.
t.Miaren: Miaren's senator was elected by Navarr at 1:30pm, immediately after standing.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold's senator was chosen by the Marcher landowners, who gathered at 1:30pm.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's senator was elected through a Urizen demos beginning at 2:00pm.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's senator was elected by the League at 2:30pm through the presentation of collected bonds.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's senator was elected by Wintermark at 2:00pm, with jars placed down for 30 minutes.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting was among the Imperial Orc titles elected by Tally of the Votes.
t.Spiral: Spiral's senator was elected by the League at 2:30pm alongside Sarvos's, through the presentation of collected bonds.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater's senator was elected by Dawn at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney.

386YE Summer Solstice interlude.d: Military units and fleets could send aid to Rachensgrab after Eska Crowspeaker's addition to the Chronicle of Heroism. League units could hunt rats in Temeschwar, Wintermark units could pursue Maarik the Golden Tongue in the Silver Peaks, and Imperial Orc and Golden Pyramid units could clear trogoni from Crimson Peak Mining. Those carrying Siakha's boons were offered a chance to slaughter Druj, Grendel or Jotun civilians. The Guerdon was set at 150 thrones, shared by units supporting the Valiant Pegasus and Wolves of War. Madruga suffered two Siakha-empowered curses and Sermersuaq prospered. Shifts in religious fortune touched Vigilance, Loyalty, the Way and Urizen's congregations. Contributions were invited for Imperatrix Lisabetta's memorial.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets continued to suffer reduced production because of the sovereign Dho'uala's rise in the Semmerlak.
n.Druj: Druj civilians were named among the targets that Siakha-blessed Imperial units and fleets might slaughter for their wealth, if enough captains took the adventure.
n.Grendel: Grendel civilians were named among the targets that Siakha-blessed Imperial units and fleets might slaughter for their wealth, if enough captains took the adventure.
n.Highguard: Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Necropolis gained income from Sarcophan visitors. Necropolis was also chosen as the site of Imperatrix Lisabetta's memorial, to be completed by the Summer Solstice.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc military units, alongside the Golden Pyramid, were invited to clear the trogoni from Crimson Peak Mining so the prospectors could claim it, earning orichalcum in the process.
n.Jotun: Jotun civilians were named among the targets that Siakha-blessed Imperial units and fleets might slaughter for their wealth, if enough captains took the adventure.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga was wracked by storms from two Siakha-empowered curses. Tharim's black frost drained Brass Coast mana sites and herb gardens until the start of the Summer Solstice, in return for steel-bound knights aiding the Fire of the South.
n.The League: Temeschwar reeled from its rat crisis as people fled the city: farms and paid-work units profited, while Lorenzo's Great Game and the Bloody Great Theatre lost their benefits. Tassato and Sarvos congregations gained income, but Holberg fleets suffered under Dho'uala.
n.Thule: After one of the Winterfolk was elected Ambassador to Otkodov, the Thule allowed Wintermark's military units to hunt Maarik the Golden Tongue in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks.
n.Urizen: Urizen's congregations lost two votes and one liao each until the start of the Winter Solstice, a consequence of the repudiation of Sulemaine. Meanwhile, Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Redoubt gained income from Sarcophan visitors.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets continued to suffer reduced production from Dho'uala. Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Karsk gained income thanks to the Sarcophan Mooring.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's military units were permitted to hunt Maarik the Golden Tongue in the Silver Peaks, with a chance for heroes to bring him to justice if a thousand force was committed. The Winterfolk of Sermersuaq also shared in the territory's newfound prosperity.

t.Holberg: Fleets based in Holberg continued to lose a rank of production to the terror of Dho'uala in the Semmerlak.
t.Karsk: Thanks to the Sarcophan Mooring, Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Karsk received an extra 18 rings from curious Sarcophan visitors.
t.Madruga: Storms wracked Madruga after the cults of Siakha performed both Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea and Thunderous Deluge, which the heroes of Anvil failed to prevent.
t.Necropolis: Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Necropolis gained extra income from Sarcophan visitors. Imperatrix Lisabetta's memorial was being raised there, to become a folly if at least ten wains were contributed.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the election of one of the Winterfolk as Ambassador to Otkodov prompted the Thule to permit the hunt for Maarik.
t.Redoubt: Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Redoubt received an extra 18 rings from Sarcophan visitors.
t.Sarvos: Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Sarvos received an extra 18 rings from Sarcophan visitors.
t.Sermersuaq: Having endured the harsh winter and Agramant's machinations, the people of Sermersuaq saw every personal resource produce an extra 22 rings until the start of the Winter Solstice. Wintermark units were also free to hunt Maarik in its Silver Peaks.
t.Tassato: Prosperity and Ambition congregations in Tassato received an extra 18 rings from Sarcophan visitors.
t.Temeschwar: With rats plaguing the city and the Unfettered Mind investigating, people left or avoided gatherings. Farms, paid-work military units and the Reapers' Repose profited, and League units could earn rings hunting rats in the sewers.
t.The Semmerlak: Dho'uala's presence in the Semmerlak continued to plague fleets with eerie encounters. It also kept prices raised for the Custodian of the Ivarsgard Docks and the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Silver Peaks became the hunting ground for Maarik the Golden Tongue, where Wintermark heroes would have a chance to bring him to justice if at least a thousand force was assigned.

386YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: Winds included Emperor Vesna's address and diplomatic updates on the Commonwealth, Jarm, the Delves, Sumaah, Asavea, Axos, Faraden and neighbouring orc nations. Appraisals covered the Sovereign Dho'uala and Sermersuaq's prosperity. Navarr and Highguard faced a final choice about the vallorn. The Children of Wrecks seized Free Landing. Holberg uncovered a cannibal conspiracy, Temeschwar's rat plague continued, and Mareave's development began. Of the major conjunctions, Wintermark defeated Jarl Idunn in Kallavesa and an Urizen-led force struck Siakha's cults in Madruga. Liathaven was left unchallenged, leaving the Green March under Jotun threat. Many lesser conjunctions defeated husks, Grendel, Jotun, vallornspawn and Dry Patricians, though scions survived in Skarsind and Karov.

n.Dawn: Dawn faced opportunities as its legacy took root in the Barrens, and Dawnish military units gained access to a vallorn-guarded trove in Brocéliande. Sites were also proposed for a memorial to the troubadour Ozren de Orzel.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named among the four orc nations surrounding the Empire, and recalled as the besiegers of the Gates of Ipotavo.
n.Grendel: Grendel raiders were slain in Spiral, Necropolis and Mareave, and the former Grendel priestess Shivaarn now leads the Children of Wrecks. The Grendel port of Oran remained closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: Highguard was called to make its choice over the final destruction of the vallorn and to pursue its peerless kinship with the Marches. Grendel were driven out of three Necropolis sites, and salvage auction rights in Arbonne were bought on Highguard's behalf.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs began transforming newly assigned Mareave, where the Golden Pyramid struck gold. At Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind, Imperial heroes suffered heavy casualties and most of the scions survived.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces lost Jarl Idunn's fight in Kallavesa and were defeated in Kahraman and Sermersuaq. Their Liathaven conjunction went unchallenged, leaving them with increased resupply there and threatening the Green March.
n.Navarr: The Navarr faced the profound decision over the vallorn and an opportunity to explore the power of wayhouses. Their efforts in the south of the Barrens began to bear fruit, and the Dance of Navarr and Thorn was performed in Hercynia.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn confronted the Children of Wrecks off Madruga and a curse on their hakima. Three Dry Patricians were destroyed in Segura and Kahraman, opening a chance to end the Blight decisively.
n.The League: The League confronted a cannibal conspiracy tied to Agramant in Holberg and the continuing rat plague in Temeschwar. It must also decide the future of Apulian, where Urizeni settlers are growing in number.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly faced a growing rift with its people and continued to seek rapprochement with Urizen. It also had to deal with the cursed Anvil of Silence. Marcher armies were bound by oaths to defend their home territories, and the Green March was left under Jotun threat.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: listed among the orc nations with which the Empire keeps careful diplomatic relations, covered further in The Price of Peace.
n.Urizen: Urizen continued its exchange of ideas with the Marches, and the rebellion in Ankra and Cinion was stabilised. Urizeni settlers are increasingly shaping Apulian, and an Urizen field marshal led the strike on Siakha's cults.
n.Varushka: A Varushkan cabalist conducted the appraisal into the Sovereign Dho'uala around the Semmerlak. In Karov, the Festering Warden and Iron Boyar were defeated, but the Haamrikoht Stone was sundered.
n.Wintermark: Iron Osric of Wintermark led the victory over Jarl Idunn, claiming the Banner of the Bear Who Swims and recovering the Sibling Swords. An appraisal proposed ways to make Sermersuaq more prosperous.

t.Bastion: Imperial heroes successfully performed Regrow the Land's Heart at Sybella Cross.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Children of Wrecks, a coalition inspired by Siakha, formed in the bay and made it impossible to challenge them without a navy.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the situation there gave the Highborn pause over kinship aid, and General Amberlain has sworn the Strong Reeds will defend it.
t.Brocéliande: Vallornspawn were slain at Black Boughs and Vale's Lament, saving thorns and opening a trove to Dawnish units.
t.Feroz: Heroes moved to intercept a suspicious Faraden agent at Morajasse, with an uncertain outcome.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: a Hahnmark magician with a peculiar boon is seeking herbalists and stormcrows at Anvil.
t.Hercynia: Vallornspawn were distracted and the Dance of Navarr and Thorn performed at Deer's Folly, but most of the boggarts at Summersend were killed.
t.Holberg: A cannibal conspiracy linked to Agramant was exposed in Holberg just as a gourmet enchantment settled over the territory.
t.Kahraman: The Jotun were defeated at Gambit and kept from resupplying Escuta, while an Irremais-marked Patrician was destroyed in the Jade Range.
t.Kallavesa: Jarl Idunn was defeated at Hvalgrunn, where the Banner of the Bear Who Swims was claimed and the Sibling Swords recovered.
t.Karov: Husk leaders were defeated at Duzekani and Malimorzi, but at Wieliczka the scions largely survived and the Haamrikoht Stone was sundered.
t.Liathaven: The chance to thwart Beater Royse was not taken, so the Jotun gained increased resupply in Liathaven and the fate of the Feni remains unknown.
t.Madruga: The Children of Wrecks hold Free Landing. A strike on Siakha's cults saw kraken eggs released along the coast and two storm curses cast on Madruga.
t.Mareave: Newly assigned to the Imperial Orcs, Mareave faces transformation, and the Golden Pyramid has struck gold there. Grendel were stopped at Eoradal, though the Brine Turtles were left alone.
t.Miaren: A meeting with the Burning Vine at Goldglades had an uncertain outcome, and a mystery of art and magic touches the territory.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos remains angry over Imperial involvement in the failure of its joint venture with the Grendel into these mountains.
t.Mournwold: The Green March was left under threat from the Jotun because the Liathaven conjunction went untaken.
t.Necropolis: Grendel were wiped out at Sanctuary Sands, Longbeach and Highrod, with an heirloom and intelligence recovered and two ghosts laid to rest.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is among those addressed by The Price of Peace.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: those travelling the Sea of Snow are flagged as interested in the Tales of Mystery.
t.Segura: Dry Patricians were destroyed at Sobral Grasses and Lucksprings, with a magician rescued and dust recovered, and the Fire Beacon remnants at Burnish were neutralised.
t.Sermersuaq: An appraisal proposed ways to make Sermersuaq more prosperous, Freydis and her Jotun were defeated at Suaq Fount, and Cathan Canae has made an offer to its people.
t.Skarsind: At Pakaanan's Pass, Imperial heroes suffered significant casualties, most of the scions survived and the force of Storm Pass was channelled.
t.Spiral: The rebellion in Ankra and Cinion was stabilised and Grendel were slain at Screed and Ossuary, while Apulian's future draws League and Urizeni interest.
t.Temeschwar: The rat plague continued as the Unfettered Mind gathered leads, leaving the Chamber of Commerce to decide how to proceed.
t.The Barrens: The Dawnish legacy is taking root amid an uneasy calm as the fate of the remaining orc septs is settled.
t.Upwold: All the boggarts at Birchland were guided home safely.
t.Weirwater: The Broken Errant was defeated at Weirmoor and all the boggarts at Wickmoor were rescued.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: Regrow the Land's Heart was performed at the Disordered Expanse.
r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Vallornspawn were slain at the Trove of Gral'athet, and Dawnish military units were given access to the trove.
r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: Vallornspawn were slain at Cara's Thicket and the thorns were saved.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: A suspicious Faraden agent was targeted at Taziolar's Woods. The outcome is uncertain, though Valens Leos may know more.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: Vallornspawn at the Toxic Dell were distracted while the Dance of Navarr and Thorn was successfully performed.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: Most of the boggarts at Merel's Glade were killed.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Jotun were defeated on the Path of Sofia, and Escuta was denied extra resupply.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: An Irremais-marked Patrician was destroyed. Nemi i Riqueza may know more about the Lasambrian champion.
r.Karov/Duzekani: The Festering Warden was defeated and its husks slain at the Broken Copse.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: The Iron Boyar was defeated and its husks slain on the Granite Path.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Imperial heroes took heavy casualties, most of the scions survived and the Haamrikoht Stone was sundered.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: The chance to thwart Beater Royse at Wyndyn Path was not taken.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Children of Wrecks have taken Free Landing. At Siakha's Maw, kraken eggs were released and Sea Mage Tuairisc survived.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Grendel were stopped from escaping the Old Skouran Orchard, and treasure was retrieved.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The opportunity to capture the Brine Turtles at Brine Blood Bay was not taken, and the situation there is unclear.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: Imperial heroes met the Burning Vine at the Old Green Fort. The outcome is uncertain, though Aniera Exiles End may know more.
r.Mournwold/Green March: The Green March is under threat from the Jotun after the Liathaven conjunction went untaken.
r.Necropolis/Highrod: The Grendel at the Coppice of Athaliah were slain and both ghosts were put to rest.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: All the Grendel at Ada's Woods were slain and their intelligence recovered.
r.Segura/Burnish: Align the Celestial Net was performed at the Ring of Dust and Glass, neutralising the remnants of the Fire Beacon.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: A Naeve-marked Patrician was destroyed at the Parched Springs, and dust was recovered.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: Gideon of the Farthest Shore was rescued and a Yoorn-marked Patrician destroyed.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Freydis and her Jotun were defeated at Hanleth's Wastes.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: At Bitter Hollow, Imperial heroes suffered heavy casualties, most of the scions survived and the force of Storm Pass was channelled.
r.Spiral/Ankra: The Urizen rebellion here was largely resolved or stabilised by the treaty with the Silver Flame.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Urizen rebellion here was largely resolved or stabilised by the treaty with the Silver Flame, though some rebels remain irreconcilable.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Grendel at Lucia's Grove were all slain and the Legacy protected.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Grendel at Sabina's Sward were all slain.
r.Upwold/Birchland: All the boggarts at James' Orchard were rescued.
r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: The Broken Errant was defeated and its husks slain at Roland's Stand.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: All the boggarts at Regan's Glade were rescued.

386YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: The Empire moved to destroy the last two Cold Sun armies, in Miaren and Hahnmark. Lasambrian Jotun pressed on in Kahraman, and other Jotun armies marched from Liath's Ring into Gravenmarch and Southmoor, where they besieged Sarcombe to restore Jarl Haakon. In Madruga, Empire, Grendel and children of wrecks fought amid a century-worst hurricane raised by Siakha's followers in Free Landing. In Mareave, a Senate compromise saw the Brine Turtles withdraw, Fleisardh claimed and Beoraidh neutral. Two Dawnish armies watched the Black Wind in the Barrens while a Druj host ravaged Therunin. Three battle opportunities were identified: Therunin, Madruga and Bregasland.

n.Dawn: Two Dawnish armies watched the Black Wind in the Barrens as its sept sought to flee. Dawn brought the largest force weight (54), and its armies cannot take the Cautious Advance or Give Ground orders.
n.Druj: A great Druj host poured out of the Sarangrave into Therunin, burning and killing. Druj forces also faced Imperial conjunctions in the Barrens, the Forest of Ulnak and Morrow.
n.Grendel: The Grendel fought the Empire and the children of wrecks for Madruga during a cataclysmic hurricane. Imperial heroes could attempt to assassinate Rahab and Questioner Polh, and face Grendel forces in Ayereed and Siluri.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: listed with a force weight of 18 for the summit's battles; a conjunction to stop wreckers was also offered in Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc control of Mareave became uncontested after the Brine Turtles withdrew. An Imperial Orc army in blizzard-struck Skarsind can take the Forge Hammers order.
n.Jotun: The Jotun attacked on three fronts: the Lasambrian Jotun in Kahraman, two armies into Gravenmarch, and western orc armies into Southmoor to besiege Sarcombe for Jarl Haakon. Imperial heroes could try to stop the Burhfæst in Bregasland.
n.Navarr: The Cold Sun's Empty Hands army remained in Miaren as the Empire moved against it, while the Druj ravaged Navarr's Therunin. Navarr brought a force weight of 50.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast faced the Lasambrian Jotun in Kahraman and a storm-wracked war with the Grendel and children of wrecks in Madruga, where many conjunctions were offered.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: listed with a force weight of 20; conjunctions were offered in League territories of Temeschwar, Sarvos and Spiral.
n.The Marches: Jotun armies marched into Southmoor in Mournwold, besieging Sarcombe. Marcher armies cannot Give Ground but gain strength fighting in their home territories, and any army may billet in Bregasland, Upwold or Mitwold.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov was named responsible for a conjunction to kill Maarik the Golden Tongue in Sermersuaq.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: listed with a force weight of 13, with conjunctions in Redoubt and Morrow and standing rules for fighting between Zenith and Morrow.
n.Varushka: Varushkan armies generate fewer victory points when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies, and can take Hospitality of the Boyars in Ossium; a conjunction against the scions was offered in Miekarova.
n.Wintermark: The Cold Sun's Silence Arc remained in Hahnmark as the Empire moved to end it. Wintermark brought a force weight of 53, and its armies can Fight with Honour and fight under special modifiers against the Jotun.

t.Ayereed: A conjunction was offered to kill the Grendel at Dunreagh's Brush in Gainmeachdubh.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the narrative crosses the Bay of Catazar to Mareave, noting the absence of storms there.
t.Bregasland: Two Jotun armies marched north from Liath's Ring into Gravenmarch. Imperial heroes could try to stop the Burhfæst at Rock Foot Wood, and Imperial armies may billet here.
t.Brocéliande: A conjunction was offered to resolve the mystery of Starstrand Steading in Boar's Dell.
t.Forest of Ulnak: A conjunction was offered to claim the stockpile at Varnalis' Cache in Grimfen Mire.
t.Hahnmark: The Cold Sun's Silence Arc remained here as the Empire moved to end the invasion, with a conjunction to stop the scions at Dun's Reach.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun continued trying to conquer the cinnabar hills, as Imperial reinforcements arrived and two more Jotun armies marched into Braydon's Jasse.
t.Karsk: A conjunction was offered to find out what was happening in the vale of Gorek's Reach.
t.Liathaven: Jotun armies marched out of Liath's Ring, two south into Kahraman and two north into Bregasland.
t.Madruga: The Empire, Grendel and children of wrecks fought here as the worst storm in a century reshaped the land. Battle and many conjunctions were offered, including to assassinate Rahab.
t.Mareave: There was no fighting: the Brine Turtles retreated south, Imperial armies claimed Fleisardh, Beoraidh became neutral and Imperial Orc control became uncontested.
t.Miaren: The Cold Sun's Empty Hands army remained here as the Empire moved to end the invasion.
t.Miekarova: A conjunction was offered to stop the scions at Biljana's Sward in Srodkoja.
t.Mitwold: Conjunctions were offered to slay Urse Longarm and to exorcise ghosts. Imperial armies may billet here, and the Drakes gain strength fighting in Mitwold.
t.Morrow: A conjunction was offered to kill the Druj and, if possible, rescue Megaris in Peregro. Urizen and Highborn armies defending Morrow from Zenith gain a bonus.
t.Mournwold: Western orc armies marched into Southmoor and besieged Sarcombe to restore Jarl Haakon, ahead of the Ore Hills rebellion's sixtieth anniversary.
t.Necropolis: A conjunction was offered to stop the wreckers at the Grove of Silence in Longbeach.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan armies can take the Hospitality of the Boyars order here.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov was named responsible for a conjunction in Sermersuaq.
t.Redoubt: Conjunctions were offered to stop the scions in Naris and defeat the Grendel in Siluri.
t.Sarangrave: A great Druj host poured out of the Sarangrave to ravage Therunin.
t.Sarvos: Conjunctions were offered to stop wreckers in Bocche and to take part in a debate at the Solare Estate in Foracci.
t.Sermersuaq: Conjunctions were offered to kill the Jotun and deal with Big and Little Icebarn in the Suaq Wastes, and to kill Maarik the Golden Tongue in the Silver Peaks.
t.Skallahn: A conjunction was offered to kill the Jotun at Auguaard's Bluff in Iron Stand.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind suffered unseasonable blizzards; Imperial Orc armies there can take the Forge Hammers order.
t.Spiral: Two conjunctions were offered to rescue citizens near Harrier's Nest in Screed.
t.Temeschwar: Conjunctions were offered to meet the Rat Kings guild and to speak with Brinton von Temeschwar in Hanuri.
t.The Barrens: Two Dawnish armies watched the Black Wind as its sept sought to flee, and a conjunction was offered to stop the Druj and the heralds of Surut.
t.Therunin: A great Druj host poured in, burning and killing; Imperial heroes could fight to prevent the slaughter at Tarn Bend.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies may billet here and the Bounders gain strength fighting in Upwold.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Highborn or Urizen armies attacking Zenith from Morrow gain a bonus to territory captured.

r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: The General of the Red Wind Corsairs was named responsible for a conjunction to kill the Grendel at Dunreagh's Brush.
r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Two Jotun armies marched in from Liath's Ring, and a battle to stop the Burhfæst at Rock Foot Wood was offered.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The Spear of the Seven was named responsible for a conjunction to resolve the mystery of Starstrand Steading.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: A conjunction was offered to claim the stockpile at Varnalis' Cache.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Tobrytan Dunning was named responsible for a conjunction to stop the scions at Dun's Reach.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Two Jotun armies marched south from Liath's Ring into Braydon's Jasse.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The Custodian of the Lost was named responsible for a conjunction at Gorek's Hollow.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: Four Jotun armies marched out of Liath's Ring, two towards Kahraman and two towards Bregasland.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The Strategos of the Brass Coast was named responsible for a conjunction at the Orchard of Tabhorios.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Siakha's followers who held Free Landing evoked the hurricane that struck Madruga; a conjunction to the Baleen Cave was offered.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The orcs of Beoraidh established their neutrality as the Brine Turtles retreated south with much of their sept.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Imperial armies claimed Fleisardh without a fight.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: A conjunction was offered to stop the scions at Biljana's Sward.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: A conjunction was offered to slay Urse Longarm at Jenny's Copse.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: A conjunction was offered to make sure the ghosts at Halebale Farm were exorcised.
r.Morrow/Peregro: A conjunction was offered at the Still Glade to kill the Druj and, if possible, rescue Megaris.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: the sixtieth anniversary of the Ore Hills rebellion falls next season.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Western orc armies besieged Sarcombe to restore Jarl Haakon, and a conjunction to trace ghosts at the Glen of Red Shadow was offered.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: A conjunction was offered to stop the wreckers at the Grove of Silence.
r.Redoubt/Naris: A conjunction was offered to stop the scions at the Tilphussian Pass.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: A conjunction was offered to defeat the Grendel at Lucia's Holt.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: A conjunction was offered to stop the wreckers at Ferocity's Stand.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra and Marta i Guerra were named responsible for a large conjunction to join a debate at the Solare Estate.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: A conjunction was offered to kill Maarik the Golden Tongue at Aino's Rest.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Conjunctions were offered to kill the Jotun and deal with Big Icebarn and Little Icebarn.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: A conjunction was offered to kill the Jotun at Auguaard's Bluff.
r.Spiral/Screed: Two conjunctions were offered to rescue citizens near Harrier's Nest.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Conjunctions were offered to meet the Rat Kings guild at Terrier's Roar and to speak with Brinton von Temeschwar at the Old Priory.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: A conjunction was offered to stop the Druj and the heralds of Surut at the Hollow Tree.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: A battle to prevent the Druj slaughter at Tarn Bend was offered.

A star is born.d: Acting on Synod judgements, the expedition found the freed slaves thriving in Leerdam. Rachensgrab's surviving common folk were living in poverty, warned by the Commonwealth never to resume slaving. Nearby, the Viyerda, humans and orcs ruled by a reincarnating Winter Queen and Summer King, hold metals and ilium but refused trade and contact. Diplomacy could be attempted through a Senate appraisal by Naomi of Virtue's Rest (60 thrones) or a Celestial Arch declaration (100 mana), but not both. Either risks angering the Commonwealth, whose ambassador objects to Imperial activity there. A judgement of rewarding could recompense the unrewarded participants. The expedition closed early.

n.Dawn: Five Dawnish fleets, including those of Caspian Du Marin and Purnelle, sacrificed their own prosperity to join the voyage. Like all participants, they went unrewarded unless the Synod or Senate chooses to recompense them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in an out-of-character note citing a television show as visual inspiration for the Viyerda, and no Grendel participants are listed.
n.Highguard: Highguard sent a modest contingent to the expedition: the military unit of Thomas and the fleet of Creed.
n.Navarr: Navarr contributed Farren Silver Streams' military unit and six fleets, among them Cadfael Silentwatch and Wyllen Blood Oak, to the voyage to the northern Sea of Steel.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast was one of the largest contributors. It sent thirteen fleets and Guillermo i Ezmara i Erigo's military unit to bring Prosperity to Rachensgrab's former slaves.
n.The League: Eight League fleets, several of them from Sarvos, and Othello di Severio von Holberg's military unit joined the expedition.
n.The Marches: The expedition answered a judgement by the Marcher Creighton Blackewater, who also sailed with his own fleet alongside four other Marcher fleets and Tom Appleseed's unit. The page closes on a Marcher proverb counselling caution.
n.Urizen: Urizen sent Hugh Ravenspire's military unit and four fleets, including Bacauda Netherwatch and Xenia, to the Sea of Steel.
n.Varushka: Varushka provided eleven fleets and Fania Vessely-Vanek's military unit, one of the larger national contributions to the flotilla.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark sent the largest contingent of any nation, with eight military units and eighteen fleets committing to the voyage.

t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the main Viyerda island is described as half the size of Sarvos, and several participating League fleets bear the name 'di Sarvos'.

An eagle in song.d: Lady Kaywenn de Orzel's writ of consecration was upheld by the Pride Assembly at the Spring Equinox 386YE. The civil service proposed an academy of music and oration with monthly martial tournaments, costing 30 wains of white granite and 90 crowns over three months, then consecrated with true liao. It would also house the High Bard and give them two thrones a season. Possible sites were Gnijezdo in Miekarova, the Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg, or Belletain in Weirwater. At the Summer Solstice the General Assembly backed Starac Sijed Orzel's mandate for Sandling (1234-248). The true liao is ready, but no work has been commissioned. The crisis of faith over Vardas blocks any extra benefits until it is resolved. The High Bard sent the Culwich Witches eighty-one names to receive gifts once the consecration is complete.

n.Dawn: The memorial honours a Dawnish troubadour and knight, and its chosen site in Weirwater would inspire pilgrims, especially the Dawnish, to look to their future and value Dawnish music. Weirwater's Culwich Witches also plan gifts for the Empire's musicians.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Ozren de Orzel is noted as having ultimately died to the Druj.
n.The League: The Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg was offered as a site that would have inspired pilgrims with League music and paid Holberg's congregations extra income, but the General Assembly chose Weirwater instead.
n.Varushka: Gnijezdo in Miekarova, where Ozren had served as a stzena and priest before his house moved to Dawn, was offered as a site honouring Varushkan music and heritage, but it was not chosen.

t.Holberg: Had the academy been built at the Pits of Ennerlund, every congregation in Holberg would have gained 36 extra rings each season, but another site was chosen.
t.Miekarova: An academy at Gnijezdo would have given every congregation in Miekarova two extra doses of liao each season, but the General Assembly chose a different site.
t.Weirwater: Chosen as the academy's site, Weirwater's congregations would each gain a Philtre of Strength every season once it is built and consecrated, though only if the crisis of faith is resolved in favour of the exemplars.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Ennerlund, home of the Great Pits left by spirits Ozren exorcised, was proposed as a monument to his Pride as a cardinal, but it was passed over.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada, site of Ozren's first congregation at Gnijezdo, was proposed for an academy that would turn pilgrims towards their past, but the mandate was not enacted.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Belletain in Sandling, where Ozren led his congregation and the Children of the Crow, was chosen for the academy. True liao is held ready, but construction has yet to be commissioned or paid for.

Another verse.d: Isaella's Dance, the Fist of the Mountains, the Tusks and the Valiant Pegasus fought in Kahraman, while a tower of black ice raised by Imperial magicians guarded Serra Damata. The Hierro, Corazón and Escuta, with the Skjaldirborn and Yantan Thetrason's warband, were pushed back from Rojota, though over five hundred Imperial soldiers died there. The Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder then struck from Liathaven into Braydon's Jasse, but the Tusks' defence gave warning in time. The western Jotun withdrew into Reinos and the northern force fell back into Liathaven. Corazón raids cost several mines resources, and the roads and kamkrags project is close to completion if Jade Range holds.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched south and east to join the fight against the Grendel in Madruga.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian armies and the reinforcing Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder were all driven out of Kahraman, falling back into Reinos and Liathaven with losses estimated at almost as many as the Empire's. The Bear who Swims was weakened by its new general's lost banner.
n.Navarr: Cadwell Waystone's Isaella's Dance pressed west against the Lasambrians, helping to win the bloody battle west of Rojota alongside a single Navarr contingent of Imperial captains.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn territory of Kahraman was liberated again, though Corazón raids cost its mines resources; the Red Wind Corsairs left to fight the Grendel in Madruga.
n.The Marches: Stanley of Chalkdown's Tusks anchored the defence, blunting the Corazón raids and giving warning of the Jotun advance from Liathaven, with a furlough in the Mournwold promised to the soldiers.
n.Wintermark: Ivar Dunning's Fist of the Mountains split its forces between the west and the Tusks in the north, and by fighting with honour saw its casualties reduced by a tenth as the Jotun offered and accepted quarter.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman was liberated after a season of hard fighting on two fronts, at a cost of nearly three and a half thousand Imperial dead or unable to fight, and its roads and kamkrags are nearly finished.
t.Liathaven: The Bear who Swims and Roaring Thunder marched out of Liathaven to seek a second beachhead in Kahraman, only to be pushed back into it.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched here to join the fight against the Grendel.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus came to Kahraman straight from fighting the scions of Cold Sun in Miaren.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks paraded south through the Mourn and were promised a furlough there by their general.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the defeated Lasambrian armies retreated through the woods back into Reinos.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Two Jotun armies with magical and allied warriors came down from Liathaven into the Jasse and fought near the site of Fort Braydon, but were held and driven back.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Lasambrian attempt to complete the conquest of Jade Range failed as they were pushed back, and the kamkrag project's completion depends on it staying in Imperial hands.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Corazón raiders struck some caravans passing through Serra Briante but could not rob the grassland folk or threaten the kamkrag labourers.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: A tower of black ice garrisoned by warriors from the realm of the Mistress of Ice and Darkness protected the peaks of Serra Damata, though the Damatian Cliffs still lost five wains of white granite to raiders.

Ashes.d: The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride watched the Black Wind army in Saltmarsh but did not engage it, and the sept fled east across the Nameless River. At least thirty-five thousand Druj poured from the Nesustak Forest into Therunin. They slaughtered Navarr defenders, seized the Thimble and the Feverwater Docks, and burned the Holt of the Oak, where almost two thousand Great Forest Orcs and Navarr died. The Arrow Vipers destroyed the Sarangrave spy network. Navarr lost control of Therunin, which is now contested, and its senator lost their seat. The Rivers of Life curse risks rousing the vallorn. A battle opportunity at Tarn Bend offered the Empire a chance to shield fleeing refugees and stop the Sephals Cauldron poisoning the land.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride held the Barrens without fighting the Black Wind, and earlier Dawnish senators had urged the Throne to veto the Rahvin treaty.
n.Druj: Seven Druj armies overran eastern Therunin with brutal efficiency, while the Arrow Vipers crushed Imperial spying in the Sarangrave. They now hold two regions of the territory and the captured Thimble and Feverwater Docks.
n.Navarr: The Navarr suffered terrible slaughter in Therunin and lost control of the territory and its Senate seat. Their survivors fled north to the Barrens, and the Holt of the Oak was lost alongside their Great Forest Orc allies.
n.Urizen: Urizen feared the Druj would press on into Lustri, where the fortification was far from complete. A Druj band also captured a Sunspire stargazer in Morrow, threatening the spire itself.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: rumours of an arrangement protecting Therunin and Brocéliande from the Druj are clearly no longer true, at least for Therunin.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The fleeing Black Wind people were ushered north into the Forest of Ulnak as they left the Barrens for the Mallum.
t.Morrow: Druj raiders captured the stargazer Megaris and threatened to loot Sunspire, and the Advisor on the Vallorn was charged with stopping them.
t.Sarangrave: The invasion of Therunin was launched from the Sarangrave. There the Arrow Vipers and the Tower of the Skink garrison destroyed the Imperial spy network and ended Imperial exploration.
t.The Barrens: The Black Wind sept crossed the Barrens peacefully under the watch of two Dawnish armies. Afterwards the territory began receiving Navarr and Great Forest Orc refugees from Therunin, and Druj with heralds of Surut moved on the Hollow Tree.
t.Therunin: The Druj conquered Eastring and East Ashes, captured the Thimble and Feverwater Docks, and destroyed the Holt of the Oak. They laid the Rivers of Life curse across the land, leaving the territory contested and the vallorn stirring.
t.Zenith: About a hundred refugees fled from East Ashes into northern Zenith, and Urizen feared a Druj push south that has not yet come.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: Black Wind bands led their fleeing people north into the Ghul'thak Forest on their way to the Mallum.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Seven Druj armies poured out of the Nesustak Forest to launch their invasion of Eastring.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Great Forest Orcs offered sanctuary to fleeing refugees, and success at Tarn Bend would see the refugees reach the protection of the Heart of Peytaht.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Gryphon's Pride resupplied here. The region risked becoming Poisoned if the Sephals Cauldron's contents were poured into the Tarn.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The Black Wind sept abandoned its homes in Murderdale to join its warriors and escape destruction.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The Black Wind army camped in sodden Saltmarsh all season until the last refugees arrived, then crossed the Nameless River into the Mallum.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Karass remained in the Bleaks, and a Druj band with heralds of Surut marched on the Hollow Tree regio to claim it for the Charred Prince.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: East Ashes fell to the Druj, and the Feverwater Docks were captured after holding for four days. A few refugees escaped south to Zenith before an eerie silence fell.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring's well-defended steadings were overwhelmed one after another, and their defenders were swiftly executed; the region is now under Druj control.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Greenheart remains vallorn-held, and the Rivers of Life curse threatens to rouse the vallorn here as refugees flee its danger.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Flame Beetle burned the Holt of the Oak and the Druj are two fifths of the way to conquering the region. Tarn Bend offered a chance to halt them and stop the region being poisoned.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Song remains in Navarr hands, but Druj forces were gathering to sweep up the Tarn Valley towards it.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Sweetglades remains vallorn-held, and the vitality of the Rivers of Life curse risks rousing the vallorn here.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: The Upper Tarn Valley is still held by the Navarr but lies in the path of the expected Druj advance up the Tarn Valley.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Urizen feared a Druj push into Lustri, whose fortification is incomplete, and the last survivors of the Sarangrave spy network emerged here.

Below the thunders.d: Seven Imperial armies, including the newly raised Narwhal's Spear, fought perhaps forty thousand Grendel and Asavean mercenaries, with Governor Rahab of Feroz present in person. Curses empowered by Siakha caused floods, monster attacks and lightning that killed around fifteen hundred and halted fighting for two weeks. The Seminary of Zemress was destroyed, the House of Guerra and Zemress Naval Academy were flooded, but the Kraken's Bane endured. Heralds of Janon helped transform the Burning Falcon, while Tharim's Winter knights left their mark on the Fire of the South. A battle opportunity at Sabadellano offered chances to kill Rahab, seize Asavean orders, rescue a defecting orc and recover a mithril map and the Star of Attar.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Eastern Sky marched west out of Dawn with the aid of the Lord of the Crossroads, resting near Summer regio that strengthened its knights and yeofolk, and arrived fit to fight in Madruga.
n.Grendel: The Grendel, supported by their armada and Asavean mercenaries, fiercely defended Siroc Plains but were slowly pushed back towards the ruins of Siroc, and their armies and navies suffered heavily from Siakha's storm. Governor Rahab was exposed to a possible assassination at Sabadellano, and his counsellor Questioner Polh was marked for death.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs left Kahraman trusting their Imperial allies to deal with the Lasambrian Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn armies fought to reclaim Madruga as their homeland was flooded and battered, losing the Seminary of Zemress and lives at the House of Guerra. The Burning Falcon was transformed by heralds of Janon, and killing Rahab offered to halve the seasonal losses of Freeborn armies for a year.
n.The League: The Wolves of War under Marcus Derivian di Sarvos fought in Madruga, and only units supporting them received shares of the Imperial Guerdon. The Apulian magnate Leann Dubh sought to bring the defecting orc Rígbarddán to Spiral, which would boost its businesses.
n.Wintermark: The new Wintermark army, the Narwhal's Spear, marched from Sermersuaq to Madruga with the help of Suaq hunters, arriving ready to fight and bolstered by Day magic.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay rose during the storm, battering coastal towns and bringing forth monsters and storm-marked pirates. A fabled map, the Dùthcha-Éadrom, was said to show a mithril mine somewhere on its shores, which the Empire might seize before Rahab claims it.
t.Feroz: Feroz's tyrannical governor Rahab left his fortified palace to fight in Siroc Plains, and the Empire was offered a chance to kill him, though he would quickly be replaced. Losing his advisor Questioner Polh would make him more unpredictable and lead him to squeeze his subjects harder.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs left Kahraman to fight in Madruga.
t.Madruga: Madruga was ravaged by Siakha's storms, which flooded its coastal settlements, killed many and destroyed the Seminary of Zemress, while the Empire advanced two-fifths of the way towards retaking Siroc Plains.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the great thunderclap over Madruga was heard as far north as Caricomare in Sarvos.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Narwhal's Spear marched from Sermersuaq to the southern coast of the Empire.
t.Spiral: If the Stone Born commander Rígbarddán defects and reaches Anvil, businesses in Spiral will be able to diversify without charge until the Summer Solstice 387YE.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos was flooded and attacked by sea monsters, sending hundreds of refugees inland, and the Seminary of Zemress was smashed to rubble by the waves.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Siakha's fane and monsters cut Free Landing off from armies unless carried by a navy, and the Freeborn Flame Marina there likely suffered major damage.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Imperial armies advanced from Lightsea into Siroc Plains, while the flooding Aleatorio and monsters from the sea struck the region during the storm.
r.Madruga/Torres: The stream beside the Crimson Drummers shrine flooded, causing lesser damage, but the Crimson Sutannir will provide no liao or money after the Summer Solstice as they support rebuilding.
r.Spiral/Apulus: A recently arrived Apulian family and magnate Leann Dubh hoped to recover their relative Rígbarddán, whose logistics skill would improve trade in and out of Apulus for a year.

Children of Wrecks.d: After Shivaarn's followers destroyed the Shining Pillar and betrayed the Asaveans, the Salt Lords denounced them. Free Landing then rejected Salt Lord rule, and the wreckers made Atalaya a haven for Siakha's worshippers. They seized Cazar Straits under Azzura di Cazarri and stormed Axiom Prison in the Iron Confederacy, freeing rogue magicians. They now raid Imperial and Grendel lands alike and are at war with the Grendel. Some Imperial citizens have defected to them. The page set out conjunctions in Madruga and Sarvos, backed by boons from Rhianos, along with opportunities to strike Jotun, Grendel and Druj holdings weakened by Siakha-blessed raids.

n.Druj: The Varnalis family of Grimfen Mire, unsettled by raids in the east of the Forest of Ulnak, were moving stores of herbs and potions. This gave Imperial heroes a chance to defeat them and take their goods and white granite.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost Free Landing's allegiance and Cazar Straits to the Children of Wrecks, who are now at war with them. Raids have also left their resupply isle of Dunreagh vulnerable to Imperial attack.
n.Jotun: Raids along the Skallahn coast drew most of the garrison away from Augaard's Bluff, leaving its weirwood stores open to an Imperial strike.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn lands in Madruga bore the brunt of the wreckers' activity. Some corsair families were rumoured to keep hidden shrines to Siakha, and the reclusive Tabhorios family appealed to Strategos Gael i Guerra for protection from a pursuing mob.
n.The League: Wreckers slipped into Sarvos to curse the territory with deadly storms from a Spring regio, threatening Aversa and the Wellspring of Jade. Stopping them fell to the Jade Custodian, Giacomo Corvinoscuro.
n.Varushka: Wagon raiders trading at the market in Ossium reported the Varnalis' movements. They offered to loot the Druj family's white granite if the Champion of Prosperity defeated them.
n.Wintermark: The icewalker Kaija Headstrong of the Narwhal's Spear scouted the wrecker mob in Madruga. Finn Vertering of Vertering Hall offered the Champion of Ambition, Eldrid Vestardottir, a share of weirwood taken from Augaard's Bluff.

t.Ayereed: Raids have left the Grendel resupply isle of Dunreagh weakly garrisoned, offering a chance to plunder 12 wains of mithril, with Asaveans expected to arrive there too.
t.Bay of Catazar: High Priestess Shivaarn claimed the whole bay for Siakha, and her ships stalk its waters, preying on Empire, Grendel, Suranni and foreign shipping alike.
t.Feroz: The Children of Wrecks seized Cazar Straits from the Grendel, leaving the southern Jewelled Isles under their control. Little more is known, since few Freeborn remain in the territory.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Raids in the east of the territory prompted the Druj Varnalis family to move their stores, exposing them to an Imperial skirmish.
t.Madruga: Free Landing now answers to the Children of Wrecks rather than the Salt Lords, and wrecker mobs roam Calvos Sound. Two conjunctions here offered chances to confront them.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the corsair Juan i Macabeo i Erigo learned of Dunreagh's weakness while visiting the new foreigners of Beoraidh.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders who trade at the stinking market in Ossium supplied the intelligence on the Varnalis.
t.Sarvos: Wreckers infiltrated the territory to unleash deadly storms that could kill people across Sarvos, though Caricomare's flood defences would limit the harm there.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: it is named as the distant, cold refuge of Howl-in-the-Night, and as the border Vertering Hall would cross to reach Augaard's Bluff.
t.Skallahn: Coastal raids drew Jotun forces away, leaving Augaard's Bluff and its weirwood stores lightly guarded.

r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: The Isle of Dunreagh, a Grendel cache of herbs, mana crystals and mithril, was left under-defended and open to assault.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Children of Wrecks claimed the region from the Grendel and turned its grand lighthouse into a shrine to Siakha under Azzura di Cazarri.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: The Varnalis family were travelling through the mire with a chest of herbs and potions, making them the target of the Champion of Prosperity, Hugh Farrier.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: A mob of wreckers and heralds plundered the pomegranate orchards, slaughtered corsairs and pursued the Tabhorios family.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The region rejected Salt Lord rule and was held by the Children of Wrecks, who made Atalaya a haven for Siakha's worshippers. A mysterious, Lock-shrouded conjunction to Baleen Cove fell to the Champion of Vigilance.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named. It is touched only by general references to wrecker activity on the Madruga coast.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn corsair was visiting the new foreigners of Beoraidh when he learned of Dunreagh's vulnerability.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Wreckers slipped into Bocche to work storm curses at the Spring regio Ferocity's Stand, endangering the hamlet of Aversa and the Wellspring of Jade.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Augaard's Bluff, near the Sermersuaq border, was left with a reduced garrison guarding weirwood, fine arms and herbs.

Construct Bounders Hall in Bregasland.d: Announced by James Forrester, Bearer of the Second Imperial Wayleave, and sponsored by the Prosperity of Morgan Townsend and Thomas Oak, the motion followed the Kith and Kin Wind of Fortune. It would have cost 12 white granite and 36 crowns, taking three months to complete. Once built, it would create the national title Bailiff of the Fens, appointed annually by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators. It would also extend the protection of the Beating the Bounds military unit action to Bregasland once Sarcombe was reclaimed from the Jotun. Thomas Oak provided 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Summer Solstice 386YE. The project lapsed, and 3 thrones 3 crowns were returned to him after the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Jotun: The Jotun conquest of Bregasland was one of the reasons the planned Bounders Hall lapsed, and the hall's Beating the Bounds benefit depended on reclaiming Sarcombe from them.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was to gain a Bounders Hall at Ottery and a Bailiff of the Fens, but the project lapsed after the territory fell to the Jotun and funding proved insufficient.

Construct City of Dreams.d: The motion framed the project as an answer to what Navarr would become once the vallorn it marches against is destroyed. It was to be self-funded through donations, costing 90 wains of weirwood, 30 wains of white granite and 360 crowns, with nine months to complete. Many citizens contributed materials and money from Summer 386YE through to Summer 388YE, with Rhys Nighthaven, Geraint Bronwen's Rest and Asthore Autumngale among the most frequent donors. Once complete, the City of Dreams will raise investment in Miaren's congregations by one, providing a vial of liao and a dose of Goosewhisper Infusion each season. It will also establish the Dreamspeaker archetype in Navarr and create the title of Dreamer's Guide.

n.Navarr: Once the city is complete, Navarr gains the Dreamspeaker archetype, and its National Assembly can appoint a Dreamer's Guide, offering the nation a vision of its future beyond the war with the vallorn.

t.Miaren: Miaren's senator proposed the motion, and once complete the city will increase investment in the territory's congregations by one, yielding liao and Goosewhisper Infusion each season.

r.Miaren/Serenael: Serenael is the site chosen for the City of Dreams, a great weirwood and white granite project funded by donations over two years.

Construct Diplomatenschloss.d: Proposed by the Senator for Casinea and seconded by Reikos, the motion passed and 50 thrones were disbursed to the Senator for Casinea. The project needed 70 white granite, 30 weirwood and 300 crowns, took six months to complete, and carries an upkeep of 5 thrones a season. Materials and money came in gradually from many contributors between Summer 386YE and Summer 387YE, with major donations from Arlais, Daughter of Mari, Solomon, and Naomi of Felix Watch. Once complete, the Ambassador to the Commonwealth again had access to mercantile support, and the Diplomatenschloss serves as a rank one fortification in Hedrossan.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a fortified Commonwealth embassy in its territory of Necropolis, built on a motion brought by its Senator for Casinea.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's Senator proposed the motion and received the 50 thrones disbursed for it, but the building stands in Necropolis.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis became home to the Diplomatenschloss, which restores the Commonwealth embassy and adds a rank one fortification to the territory.

r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: The completed Diplomatenschloss stands in Hedrossan as the Commonwealth's fortified embassy and serves as a rank one fortification there.

Construct Great Hall of Fabric Arts.d: Announced by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, with the backing of the Varushkan Assembly through a mandate enacted by Anatolij Paukov Zorkin, the commission cost 80 white granite and 240 crowns and took six months to complete. Funding came over several seasons into Spring 387YE: Varushkan citizens provided granite and thrones each season, alongside donations from Triska Markova, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Kostjya, Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven, a large contribution from Yakov "Yasha" Bjelovuk, and small gifts. Once complete, the hall would spark a renaissance in the fabric arts, reminding Varushkans of their traditional heritage and restoring these skills to prominence in the nation's culture.

n.Varushka: The hall was meant to start a renaissance in Varushkan fabric arts, restoring these traditional skills to prominence in the nation's culture. The Varushkan Assembly backed the motion and Varushkan citizens supplied much of the granite and money.

t.Karov: The Great Hall of Fabric Arts was to be built in Delev in Karov, making the territory home to the centre of Varushka's revived fabric arts.

Construct Journeymage Towers.d: Proposed by Semmerholm's senator and seconded by Karov's, the motion answered the Less welcome tenants wind of fortune. It cost 24 white granite, 72 crowns and three months to complete, and 60 thrones were disbursed to the Senator for Semmerholm. The Wisdom Assembly backed it through a mandate enacted by Kalina Jadwigowna Piosnkowa Prochnost. Many citizens contributed after the Summer Solstice, including Triska Markova, Amicia of the Semmerlak, and Varushkan, League and Dawn citizens. Once the towers were complete, the threat to Semmerlak ships was resolved and the Wavewatchers sodality was firmly established. The Senate then created the title of Watcher of the Semmerlak at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senator for Semmerholm proposed the motion and received the funds, and Dawn citizens gave 6 crowns and 2 wains of white granite towards the towers protecting Semmerlak shipping.
