n.Varushka: Varushka hosted two of the three towers, in Karov and Ossium. Karov's senator seconded the motion, and Varushkans such as Triska Markova and other citizens supplied much of the granite and coin.

t.Karov: Karov's senator seconded the motion, and a Journeymage Tower was built in its Malimorzi region to guard ships from Dho'uala.
t.Ossium: A Journeymage Tower was raised in Ossium's Bittershore region as part of the network that ended the threat to Semmerlak shipping.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's senator proposed the motion and received the 60 thrones, and a tower was built in Lacre, ending the Dho'uala threat to ships on the Semmerlak.

r.Karov/Malimorzi: Malimorzi became the site of one of the three Journeymage Towers that together removed the danger posed by Dho'uala.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore received one of the Journeymage Towers, helping to secure the Semmerlak's waters for shipping.

Construct Orchard of the Watch.d: The senator for Mournwold proposed the motion and the senator for Necropolis seconded it. It passed with the backing of the Pride Assembly, through a statement of principle raised by Friar John of the Mourn. The cost set by the opportunity was 10 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. Friar John supplied all of it after the Summer Solstice. Once the orchard was finished, Greensward gained the memorial quality: while the trees stand, the angry ghosts remaining there will not trouble the living. If the orchard is ever destroyed, the ghosts will rise again, likely furious, and their wrath will probably fall on whoever destroyed it.

n.The Marches: A Marcher priest, Friar John of the Mourn, paid for the orchard and won the Pride Assembly's support for it. The result calms the angry ghosts haunting Marcher land in Greensward.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold's senator proposed the motion. The completed orchard now keeps the territory's restless dead in Greensward from troubling the living.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: Greensward gained the memorial quality: its angry ghosts will not trouble the living while the orchard stands, but destroying the trees risks unleashing their fury.

Construct Reeds Roost.d: Bregasland's senator proposed the motion and Upwold's seconded it. It commissioned a sinecure called Reed's Roost in Bildewold in the North Fens of Bregasland, producing mana crystals each season. The commission cost 10 mithril and 30 crowns on top of standard costs, and the work took three months. After the Summer Solstice 386YE, Willem Tarne provided 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns. The sinecure is now complete. The post of Roost's Reeve is filled annually, and appointment requires the unanimous decision of the Marcher senators.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page and are linked only because they held part of Bregasland at the time.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained a mana-producing sinecure in Bregasland and a new national title, Roost's Reeve, which their senators must agree unanimously to appoint each year.

t.Bregasland: The sinecure of Reed's Roost was commissioned and completed in Bildewold, Bregasland, at the proposal of the territory's own senator.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The North Fens became home to Reed's Roost, a completed sinecure producing mana crystals each season.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Ayereed.d: Dugdale's announcement declared the Empire the true masters of the Bay of Catazar and proclaimed the time of the Salt Lord over. The cove required 10 white granite, 30 crowns and three months' work, but only seven crowns were donated, by Llandun Waystone, Rhys Nighthaven, Triska Markova and Protectorate Kardak. Shortly after the Winter Solstice 386YE, mercenaries paid by Maistir Varden overran the area and the work was abandoned. In Spring 387YE Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo announced a new cove in Ayereed, together with decommissioning the spy network in Sarangrave. Karrak provided 3 thrones, 6 crowns and 10 wains of white granite. Once complete, fleets would be able to support the cove as military units support spy networks.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the later Spring 387YE announcement decommissioned the Imperial spy network in Sarangrave, a territory the Druj held.
n.Grendel: The Imperial Spymaster targeted Grendel-held Ayereed, vowing to wrest the Bay of Catazar from the Grendel yoke and declaring the time of the Salt Lord over.

t.Ayereed: The Empire tried to build a smugglers cove in Ayereed, but work was abandoned after the Winter Solstice 386YE when Maistir Varden's mercenaries overran the area. A second attempt was announced in Spring 387YE.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Spymaster's announcement claimed the Empire as the true masters of the Bay of Catazar and vowed to wrest it from Grendel control.
t.Sarangrave: The Spring 387YE announcement called for the Imperial spy network in Sarangrave to be decommissioned alongside the new cove in Ayereed.

Construct Statue Commemorating Conquest.d: The announcement celebrated the liberation of Ossium and the bringing of the Way to the Empire's first new territory in three centuries. The folly cost 3 white granite, 1 weirwood, 1 mithril and 15 crowns, and took three months to build. The motion said it was fully funded by prosperous Ossian citizens. After the Summer Solstice, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov provided the mithril, weirwood, white granite and 7 crowns. Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh gave 4 crowns, and Ivana Petara Vodjavic, Velko Perunovich Razoradze, Rhys Nighthaven and Kostjya gave one crown each. The completed statue, the Pride of Ossium, now stands in Lomaa.

n.Varushka: Varushkans led the commemoration of their liberation of Ossium, and Bolotnikov and other Varushkan donors paid for most of the statue that now marks the Way's arrival in the territory.

t.Ossium: Ossium gained the Pride of Ossium, a monument celebrating its liberation as the first new Imperial territory in 300 years.

r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The completed Pride of Ossium statue now stands at Lomaa in the Galath Fields.

Construct Vicente School and Orphanage.d: The ministry cost 12 mithril and 36 crowns, plus possible Black Plateau costs pending a mandate regarding the Block, and took three months to build. It shelters orphans and trains them as reckoners and traders with help from those across the city, while purchasing mana crystals. It also creates the tenured League title of Custodian of the Vicente School and Orphanage, appointed by the League's Senators and revocable by the League National Assembly. After the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox, donors including Bella, Francisco and Fiorente Vicente d'Apulian, Heliodoro Vicente, Otmar van Holberg, Teodore duSesna and Serenus Starsong supplied the mithril and money. The Custodian could first be appointed, by unanimous decision of the League Senators, at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.The League: The League gained a new tenured national title, the Custodian of the Vicente School and Orphanage, appointed unanimously by its Senators and revocable by its National Assembly. Members of the Vicente family were among the main funders.

t.Spiral: Spiral, held by the League, gained a mana ministry that shelters orphans, trains them as reckoners and traders and purchases mana crystals.

r.Spiral/Apulus: The Vicente School and Orphanage was built in Apulian in Apulus, giving the city an orphanage for training reckoners and traders and a mana trading house.

Digging for fire.d: Dozens of Golden Pyramid magicians explored Mareave, a land few Imperial citizens had seen except as slaves. In Nadir they found a shifting regio among Urizen ruins, holding two bronze bowls that produce three vis each season. Dubbed the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons, this sinecure could be set up by the Senate as an Imperial or Imperial Orcs position. Imperial Orcs running mines in Mareave now earn 30 extra rings a season. The Grandmaster could commit the order to stay a year for ingots, mana and cerulean mazzarine each season. The order also proposed a Grand Lodge in Clisearn, which the Senate would need to approve.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Mareave is described as lying on the frontier with the Grendel, one reason it is suggested for a Golden Pyramid grand lodge.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs who run mines in Mareave gain 30 extra rings each season. The Bronze Bowls could become a national Imperial Orcs position, and the Golden Pyramid could commit to exploring Mareave alongside them for a year.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: trade through Beoraidh might open access to luxuries from Madruga.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League magicians were among those who surveyed Mareave's mines, and Beoraidh's trade might reach Sarvos.
n.Urizen: Old Urizen spires in Icarion and Nadir drew Golden Pyramid explorers, and one ruined spire in Nadir held the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons, decorated with astronomantic sigils.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction follows two Wintermark prospectors who earned more in Mareave than a month's work in Hahnmark would bring.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the fiction's prospectors compare their Mareave profits with what they would earn in Hahnmark.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh's trade across the bay could give access to luxuries from Madruga.
t.Mareave: Mareave proved rich in ores and all four magic metals. Its mines now pay Imperial Orc operators 30 extra rings a season, a vis-producing minor wonder was found there, and the Golden Pyramid may stay on or build a grand lodge in the territory.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh's trade across the bay could give access to luxuries from Sarvos.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: unlike Skarsind, Mareave was terra incognita to most Imperial citizens.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Golden Pyramid magicians held trade talks with the folk of Beoraidh, a neutral city-state whose trade across the bay could bring luxuries from Madruga, Sarvos and beyond if negotiations go well.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn's Fundindelve already yields mithril, and the order proposed a Grand Lodge on estates in Clisearn, between Beoraidh and the Fundindelve, costing 20 white granite, 20 mithril and 15 thrones.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Most of Mareave's Urizen ruins stand in Icarion's foothills, and Golden Pyramid magicians explored them with paid local orc guides.
r.Mareave/Nadir: High in Nadir's hills, magicians found a ruined spire holding a shifting regio and the Bronze Bowls of the Three Seasons. The bowls produce three pawns of prismatic ink, vital honey or heart's blood depending on the season, awaiting a Senate decision on who receives them.

Drumbeat of war.d: Asavea, which declared war after the razing of Chalonsio, continues to back the Grendel with warships and troops, and two more warships were sighted at Dubhtraig. Imperial missionaries ended any hope of peace. The General Assembly enacted mandates creating the Anchor the Way in Asavea commission (750 wains of white granite, 280 Thrones) and focusing missionary effort on Asavea. The Freeborn Assembly urged captains to smuggle the Way there, and the Conclave backed the Sevenfold Path reaching out to Asavean magicians. The Highborn Assembly kept its resources on the Grand Inspiration in Bastion. The Asavean bounty cut Imperial taxation by 62 thrones a season, though Imperial fleets trading with Sumaah, the Commonwealth and the Sarcophan Delves gained a rank.

n.Grendel: The Grendel kept receiving Asavean warships, mercenaries and warbands, and a Grendel company landed in Naris with Asaveans to raze the Academy of Arms. An alternative mandate to send missionaries to the Broken Shore and Attar was proposed but not chosen.
n.Highguard: Highborn wayfarers led the missionary effort in Asavea, but the Highborn Assembly chose not to divert white granite and crowns from the Grand Inspiration of the Way to the Asavean commission.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are cited, alongside the Grendel, as a minor power by comparison with Asavea.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly enacted a mandate urging ship captains to carry missionaries and aid to Asavea, opening the Smuggle the Way to Asavea opportunity to Freeborn fleets. The Brass Coast's Asier i Elia i Guerra is ambassador to Asavea.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the foreign nations an unchosen worldwide missionary mandate would have reached, and would have seen as a challenge to its sovereignty.
n.Urizen: Grendel raiders and Asaveans landed in Naris to attack the Academy of Arms, and the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine, Limonos of the Astral Observatory, was charged with defeating them. Mandates without a greater majority would not influence Urizen.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: mandates that failed to win a greater majority would not influence the people of Varushka.

t.Bastion: The Highborn Assembly chose to keep white granite and crowns flowing to the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion rather than send them to Asavea.
t.Bay of Catazar: Three great Asavean warships, Balo's Grace, Leaping Bull and Wind Tamer, operate in the bay supporting the Grendel, but Asavean bounty-hunters were not yet willing to sail the bay in force to attack Imperial trade.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: rumour holds that the Asavean destruction of the Isle of Osseini and Shantarim was done at the behest of Governor Rahab of Feroz.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Asavean warships have been identified supporting the Grendel navies in Madruga.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was named as a destination for missionaries under an unchosen worldwide mandate, and was expected to treat it as a challenge to its sovereignty.
t.Redoubt: A Grendel warship landed raiders and Asaveans in Naris to target the Academy of Arms as revenge for Imperial missionaries in Asavea.

r.Redoubt/Naris: A company of Grendel with Asaveans landed in Naris, bypassed wealthy spires and marched on the Academy of Arms. They threatened to slaughter pilgrims and students and to wreck the palaestra unless the Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine defeated them.

Famine and feast.d: The Lictors agreed to a very formal parley and offered to sustain Scrivener's Bloodmark contracts in exchange for ilium. Ossegrahn agreed to parley, offering thanks and questioning Navarr ties to Arhallogen. Rhianos declined parley, empowered Golden Voyage and began a year-long race to the four corners of the world. Kimus declined parley but offered a boon of finding for Gilda Ashwine's grave or Emperor Frederick's Pauper's Key. Sung sent heralds to trade boons for vision interpretations and eased Clear Counsel of the Everflowing River. Blood-on-the-Snow demanded an oath before parleying and offered boons through Crimson Letters. The Archmage of Winter swore no oath, so that parley failed.

n.Dawn: Ossegrahn wished to thank those who protected the Tarnfather's charges on the expedition to Dawn, to meet Ser Elienne of Dawn over an act of profound healing, and he condemned the recent bloodshed in the Barrens.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Blood-on-the-Snow's herald cited wishing for the Druj to all die in a fire as an example of a boon not worth requesting.
n.Grendel: Rhianos took an interest in the Grendel as a sworn enemy of Siakha, and offered boons to anyone taking part in the four conjunctions of the Sentinel Gate at the coming Solstice.
n.Highguard: Kimus revealed that Gilda Ashwine's remains, once interred in a basilica in Bastion, were secretly reburied after she lost her exemplar status. The eternal offered to find the grave if the Conclave asked, and Ossegrahn refused to raise forests over the meadows and orchards of Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Kimus advised that the orc researcher Snowstorm Henk, commissioned to explore the Sorrowful Tunnels in Skarsind, would be better served by an investigator sent by Walker on the Littoral, because the servants of secrets might take offence at the delving.
n.Navarr: Ossegrahn summoned the Hand of the Healers and the Granger of the Golden Orchard to explain why the Navarr seemed to be allying with the children of the Spider King. He warned that he was reconsidering his patronage of the Houses of Healing.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Ossegrahn's message was carried by a Freeborn hakima, and Rhianos pointed to the extended docks at the Great Harbour of Elos as a means to raise a navy.
n.The League: Ossegrahn refused to displace the natural life of Sarvos's grasslands and orchards to raise forests for ward-making. Kimus noted that the lost Pauper's Key was the work of the artisan Catherine de Sarvos.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Willowbraid was curious about the Archmage of Spring's suggestion that they travel together to the lands of the Thule to feed their people.
n.Urizen: Ossegrahn declined to help with Urizen's cursed mana sites, saying crystal mana is not essential to life. Blood-on-the-Snow invited magicians able to cast Crimson Letters, a ritual of Urizen lore, to use it to request his boons.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene features a civil servant, Jorgen, who knows Wintermark well, and Kimus noted that the Gildenheim runeforge was moved to Runegrott in Hahnmark.

t.Bastion: Kimus recounted that Gilda Ashwine's remains were once interred in a basilica in Bastion before the civil service disinterred and secretly reburied them.
t.Bay of Catazar: Rhianos had lost interest in raids across the Bay and dismissed a race around it as too small. The eternal said an Imperial navy raised on the Bay would be the moment to seek their boons.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the Gildenheim runeforge was noted as having been dismantled and moved to Runegrott in Hahnmark.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos suggested the Empire could use the extended docks at the Great Harbour of Elos to raise a navy.
t.Necropolis: Ossegrahn refused to kill and displace the meadows and orchards of Necropolis to raise forests for Imperial ward-making.
t.Sarvos: Ossegrahn named the grasslands, meadows and orchards of Sarvos as rich with life and refused to replace them with forests for magicians' convenience.
t.Skarsind: Kimus discussed the Sorrowful Tunnels, which Snowstorm Henk had been commissioned to explore. The eternal advised seeking an investigator from Walker on the Littoral to protect the delving.
t.The Barrens: Ossegrahn condemned the recent violence in the Barrens and vowed to work so that such actions never happen again. He thanked those who saved creatures driven into the Empire by the Merciless One.

Farm, fur, and fish.d: Graciana found that Sermersuaq already paid its way and was recovering from the Jotun invasion. She suggested a further appraisal to reopen Pakaanan's Pass to Skarsind, and proposed revisiting the Thule offer to hunt in Suaq Fount and East Floes, perhaps by moving the Thule embassy to Sermersuaq. Her commission proposals included gardens and a lodge at the Hot Springs of Taniki, and a fishery and a tradehall at Atalaq. A Mediator of Atalaq could redirect the benefits of these works. To ease the treasury, she suggested decommissioning the Jotun-built castles in favour of beacons, or relinquishing the Pride of Ikka's Tears. Two Jotun warbands were hunting the returning Icebarn Twins.

n.Imperial Orcs: Reopening Pakaanan's Pass could let Skarsind trade its wood and metal for Sermersuaq's meat, fish, herbs, furs and ivory, to the benefit of both nations. Their herbalists might also gain from proposed cerulean mazzarine gardens at Taniki.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces sealed Pakaanan's Pass in 383YE and built the costly Sermersuaq castles. Two Jotun warbands were moving to intercept the Icebarn Twins and claim the items embedded in them.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Great Mine of Briante in Kahraman is cited as the model for relinquishing the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
n.The League: Graciana visited the Imperial mint in Tassato and drew inspiration from Temeschwar's Reaper's Repose. A proposed Atalaq Tradehall would let the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage bring Sermersuaq's exotic meats to League cities for 7 crowns a season.
n.Thule: Graciana suggested a Wintermark ambassador could revisit the Thule request to hunt in Suaq Fount and East Floes, perhaps by moving the Thule embassy to Sermersuaq. A trade ministry could then exchange furs and meat for Thule vis or raw materials, though current tensions must first be resolved.
n.Varushka: The Thule embassy could be moved out of Mieriada to Sermersuaq. Varushkan herbalists also share the difficulty of growing cerulean mazzarine in cold climes that the Taniki gardens would address.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark proposed the appraisal, and it offered many ways to enrich Sermersuaq, including Atalaq great works, a Mediator of Atalaq, Taniki sinecures and fleet trade bonuses. Ways to raise its contribution to the treasury included beacons or giving up the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: its beacons are cited as a model for Sermersuaq, and the old Gulnar's Deephall mithril proposal there might be revisited.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: its Great Mine of Briante, which brings in over 400 Thrones a year, is cited as a comparison for relinquishing the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its beacons, used without fortifications, are cited as the model for Sermersuaq's proposed beacons.
t.Miekarova: The Thule embassy currently stands in Miekarova, and Graciana suggested a single Senate motion and commission could move it to Sermersuaq.
t.Otkodov: The orcs of Otkodov might be offered hunting rights in Sermersuaq in exchange for vis, mana or raw materials, though relations are currently on a knife edge.
t.Sermersuaq: The territory was the subject of the appraisal, which proposed fisheries, a tradehall, gardens, a lodge, beacons, trade with neighbours and treasury savings. The Icebarn Twins were also due to emerge there during the Summer Solstice.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind's trade with Sermersuaq remains blocked by the collapsed Pakaanan's Pass. Reopening it would require a further appraisal, but could benefit both territories.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Graciana spent a few days visiting the Imperial mint there before heading north.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: its Reaper's Repose lodge inspired Graciana's proposal for the Hot Springs Hall.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The Thule embassy at Wendell's Hope in Mieriada could be relocated to Sermersuaq, which is easier for the orcs of Otkodov to reach.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Thule had asked to hunt in East Floes, and Graciana suggested the request be revisited and the Thule embassy perhaps moved nearby.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Atalaq in Sealtoq would host the proposed Atalaq Fishery, Atalaq Tradehall and a Mediator of Atalaq. The proposed Beacons of Sermersuaq would also be sited here, operating as long as Atalaq remains Imperial.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the Silver Peaks are noted as rich in weltsilver and tempest jade that the Thule might trade.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Thule had asked to hunt in Suaq Fount, which is easy for them to reach and a possible new home for the Thule embassy.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Icebarn Twins were due to emerge from Sydanjaa in the Suaq Wastes during the Summer Solstice, pursued by two Jotun warbands. Liv Tidgaring and Derowen were responsible for stopping the warbands.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The Hot Springs of Taniki could host the Gardens of Taniki, growing cerulean mazzarine, and a Hot Springs Hall lodge. The Hall would spur new businesses and add two thrones to Sermersuaq's taxation.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The pass, sealed by a Jotun force in 383YE, is impassable to armies and caravans. Graciana recommended a separate appraisal to reopen it for military and merchant use.

For the Common Good.d: Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen reported that the war with Jarm had left the Commonwealth on the back foot against Jarmish magic. They asked for Imperial mercenaries, which would need a Senate motion. They warned that any further military rituals given to Jarm would breach the Liberty Pact, which they believed was doomed by Axos's vote. They offered a fortified embassy to replace the one the Grendel destroyed in Madruga, and an ilium-selling ministry, the Sternenmetal Tower. They also voiced suspicion of Imperial interest in Rachensgrab and thanked the Empire for a storm warning and the Gatekeepers for their restraint. The Senate built the diplomatenschloss in Necropolis. The Sternenmetal Tower remained available until the end of Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Grendel: The Grendel destroyed the Commonwealth embassy in Madruga when Siroc burned, and their violent presence in the Bay of Catazar made trade there difficult. The new embassy was offered as a fortification partly so it would be harder for them to destroy.
n.Highguard: The Senate chose Highguard's territory of Necropolis for the new Commonwealth diplomatenschloss, an embassy that doubles as a fortification garrisoned by Commonwealth soldiers.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost the Commonwealth embassy in Madruga when the Grendel burned Siroc, where Commonwealth soldiers had died alongside them. Freeborn corsairs had helped keep Bay of Catazar trade going until the storm warning drove Commonwealth merchants elsewhere.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were cited as a nation the Empire deals with on its own terms, and as a possible future Liberty Pact member the Commonwealth feared would dilute its voice.
n.Urizen: The Commonwealth insisted that its new embassy must not be built in Urizen's Redoubt, fearing the danger of placing it close to the Jarmish embassy.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Commonwealth wanted its new embassy somewhere on the Bay because it was easiest to reach, despite the area being a Grendel-infested warzone. Commonwealth shipping there fell sharply after the Imperial warning of magical storms.
t.Madruga: The old Commonwealth embassy in Madruga had been destroyed by the Grendel when Siroc burned, prompting the plan to build a replacement.
t.Necropolis: The Senate commissioned the Commonwealth diplomatenschloss in Necropolis. It was to be both an embassy and a rank one fortification garrisoned by Commonwealth soldiers.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was explicitly ruled out as a site for the new Commonwealth embassy because of the risk of placing it near the Jarmish embassy.

Fortify Gildenheim.d: Announced in Summer 386YE by Groza, Legion Engineer, the commission took up the opportunity from the Standing in the sun wind of fortune. It benefited from a mandate enacted by Viviane Barossa de Coeurdefer. The cost was 48 white granite, 16 mithril and 240 crowns, with the crowns paid in full by the Tamazi, and the work takes a year to complete. Irontide Flax supplied the 16 wains of mithril and 48 wains of white granite after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. Once complete, Gildenheim will be protected by a rank one fortification of 3000 strength that takes only half the normal damage from magical attacks such as Thunderous Tread of the Trees.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' territory of Skarsind gains a warded fortification at Gildenheim, strengthening their hold against military and magical assault once the year-long construction finishes.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind is to receive a rank one fortification of 3000 strength at Gildenheim, with Tamazi runic wards halving damage from magical attacks such as Thunderous Tread of the Trees.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Gildenheim in Gildermark is the site of the new fortification, with materials supplied by Irontide Flax after the Autumn Equinox and completion due a year after the commission.

Fortify Vigilant Swan.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Hercynia, the motion called for improving the Vigilant Swan into a 3000-strong fortification defending Riverwatch, with no upkeep and no commission required. It cost 20 mithril, 20 ilium and 120 crowns, and took six months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Shiloh provided the 20 rings of ilium, 20 wains of mithril and 14 thrones 7 crowns, with Farren Silver Streams adding a further crown. The work is now complete, and Riverwatch is defended by the Swans of Alabaster and Onyx fortification.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a new fortification, the Swans of Alabaster and Onyx, strengthening its defence of Reikos, with the construction materials and most of the money supplied by Shiloh.

t.Reikos: Reikos's own senator proposed the motion, and the territory now has a 3000-strong fortification built around the Vigilant Swan bourse seat.

r.Reikos/Riverwatch: Riverwatch is now defended by the Swans of Alabaster and Onyx, a 3000-strong fortification raised at the Vigilant Swan that needs no upkeep.

Guide the spirit.d: Relations were stable but strained. The Sumaah wanted Axos expelled from the Liberty Pact, distrusted the new Doctrine of Enlightenment, and curbed bulk liao sales. They welcomed the ban on Ocean's Caress and Imperial help against the Asavean blockade of Zemeh. They sought Senate or Throne permission to give Ambassador Accalon an apology gift, offered sympathy over Siroc, and sent delegates to discuss recognising Amika and Alberto Acciai. Wreckers serving Siakha ran the Swift Eagle aground in Longbeach and seized the präst Kauitalic, whom Accalon was charged to rescue. The Conclave disseminated Hammers of the Brilliant Shore and Stalwart Stand on Solid Ground. The assembly mandates meant every nation except Varushka and Urizen could aid Sumaah.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah cited Axos's alliance with Grendel slavers to attack Tsark as proof of Axou insincerity about ending slavery.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Accalon, the Imperial Ambassador to Sumaah, was charged with rescuing the kidnapped präst Kauitalic and was the intended recipient of a Sumaah apology gift. Highborn fleets, already fighting Asaveans in the Sea of Salt, were praised by the Sumaah and needed no mandate to continue.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sumaah trading vessels had become noticeably absent from the docks of Sarvos.
n.Urizen: Urizen was one of only two nations whose fleet captains could not join the effort to help the Sumaah against Asavean pirates and privateers after the assembly mandates passed.
n.Varushka: Varushka was one of only two nations whose fleet captains could not join the effort to help the Sumaah against Asavean pirates and privateers after the assembly mandates passed.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly passed a mandate by greater majority (309-0), sending Rafe with 50 doses of liao to urge Wintermark's sailors and fleet captains to help the Sumaah resist Asavean pirates.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the split in the Way was framed as reducing animosity between pilgrims who look to Bastion and those who look to Timoj.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: ongoing problems in the Bay of Catazar were noted alongside the decline in Sumaah trading ships reaching Imperial ports.
t.Necropolis: The Sumaah ship Swift Eagle was boarded and run aground on the Necropolis coast. Wreckers following High Priestess Shivaarn carried off the präst Kauitalic to sacrifice to Siakha, prompting a rescue mission through the Sentinel Gate.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the brightly coloured sails of Sumaah traders had been noticeably absent from the docks of Sarvos.

r.Necropolis/Longbeach: In Longbeach, the Children of Wrecks ran the Swift Eagle aground, threw most of its crew overboard and dragged the bound präst Kauitalic ashore. A rescue mission led by the Ambassador to Sumaah was called for, with Rhianos offering boons to those who fought there.

How the sausage is made.d: Following Spring Equinox statements by Paulus Adelaar van Holberg and Prince Bishop Jonah Yakovitch, the new Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage, Kanute Adelaar van Holberg, became a sought-after arbiter of good food, and the title now attracts 5 crowns a season while free of scandal. Vigilance led magistrates to pie-makers on Flotilla Street and the Holmauer Park Howler, cultists empowered by Agramant's boons; they were executed, but no malefactor was found and a ledger of pseudonymous buyers hints at a deeper conspiracy. Jonah also revealed that Divina Inquilina di Tassato Regario of the Childer of the Black Drop survives. The League and Vigilance assemblies may enact mandates to hunt the cannibals in Holberg or across the Empire.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highrod lemon zest, called the best in the Empire, appears among the delicacies the enchanted gourmands of Holberg sought out.
n.The League: League citizens embraced the Custodian of the Bloody Great Sausage as a guide to safe victuals, while reeling from news of Agramant cannibals in Holberg and the survival of the Black Drop magician Divina; the League National Assembly may mandate a hunt for the conspiracy's ringleaders, who will otherwise escape.

t.Holberg: A Night enchantment drew Holberg's people towards exotic food just as Agramant's cannibal cultists were uncovered there, likely leading some unwitting diners to the butchers; several cultists were caught and executed but the conspiracy's centre remains hidden.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: lemons from Highrod in Necropolis are cited as an imported luxury sought by Holberg's enchanted gourmands.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: In Holmauer Park a courting couple found a gold ring in a sausage, and the sausage seller, the Holmauer Park Howler, froze would-be captors with a terrible howl before bravos tackled him; his source of meat remains unknown.
r.Necropolis/Highrod: Mentioned in passing: Highrod is named as home of the best lemons in the Empire, whose zest featured in Holberg's enchanted feasting.

In the hills, the cities.d: The Axou still blamed the Empire for their losses in the failed 384YE raid on the Mountains of the Moon. They accepted reparations but refused any military cooperation. The Empire's blocking of Commonwealth and Sumaah efforts to expel Axos from the Liberty Pact was welcomed even by hostile citadels. In Kaban, Ilarch Kyther Deianeira, allied with the scholar Theodosia and advocating Nikitis Axou unification, offered to have a priest hallow one item to Understanding (Peace) for each Assembly of the Nine member who swore to bear it for a year. In return the Ilarch sought 100 doses of liao, safe conduct and a thank-you letter from the Throne. Separately, Ilarch Maxatios offered 18 crowns a wain for up to fifty wains of white granite this season and next.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj siege of the Gates of Ipotavo, lifted by the Empire, is recalled, and the Axou are said to want the Druj destroyed and might move against them if they were fatally weakened, but not in coordination with the Empire.
n.Grendel: The Grendel Paymaster Muireall's 384YE proposal of a joint raid on the Mountains of the Moon lay at the root of the Tsark Debacle, in which the Grendel suffered heavy losses after Tsark was apparently forewarned.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Ambassador to Axos is listed as Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr.

t.Mountains of the Moon: The white granite-rich Tsark passes were the target of the failed 384YE Grendel and Axou raid, whose collapse with heavy losses still poisoned Axou relations with the Empire.

Inextricable, indefatigable, and inevita.d: Using the Throne's power to speak to the whole Empire, carried across the land by the civil service, Emperor Vesna praised the Military Council for adding three territories in a few years: Ossium, the Barrens and most recently Mareave. The Emperor called land one of the Empire's most valuable assets, won with Imperial lives, and urged citizens to settle and live virtuously in it. Vesna denounced anyone who curses an Imperial territory to harm its citizens as no friend of the Empire, deserving the sack and sword, and applauded those in Anvil seeking a better path. Citing the Legacy of the First Empress and the Synod's expansion of doctrine, the Emperor set the ambitious goal that no corner of the Empire be anything less than a shining example of Prosperity.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named, but the Barrens, which it holds, is praised as one of three territories recently brought into the Empire.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Mareave, which it holds, is hailed as the most recent territory added to the Empire.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named, but Ossium, which it holds, is listed among the territories recently added to the Empire.

t.Mareave: The Emperor named Mareave as the most recent territory won by the Military Council, a land where lost souls might now find the Way and where citizens are urged to settle and prosper.
t.Ossium: The Emperor named Ossium as one of three territories added to the Empire in recent years, a place now offered to citizens as a new home in which to find Prosperity.
t.The Barrens: The Emperor named the Barrens among the territories recently brought into the Empire, holding it up as land won with Imperial lives that citizens should put to virtuous use.

Kith and kin.d: Nigel Hornbeam's unanimous judgement asked the Highborn to help the beaters patrol Marcher borders. Two mandates became possible: Marcher beaters could hunt the traitor Dalton Royse, and the Highborn unconquered could spoil Jotun supply caches in Southmoor. Plans for the Bailiff of the Downs to organise paid beaters stalled when Bounders Hall in Sarcombe fell to the Jotun. The Empire could build Bounders Halls in other Marcher territories, fortify Southmoor with the Third Pie, or build an unbreakable fort at Fishers Rock in Bregasland. Highguard's peerless kinship was extended by two seasons. Jotun ghosts appeared at Halebale Farm in Oddmire. James Forrester used a Wayleave to commission a Bounders Hall in Bregasland.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly could mandate its unconquered to spoil Jotun caches in Southmoor. Its peerless kinship was also extended by two more seasons, and it could now name the aid it would offer without waiting for the other nation's assembly.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces had invaded the Mournwold, exploiting Jarl Haakon's supply caches and Dalton Royse's intelligence. They captured Bounders Hall in Sarcombe and threatened Bregasland.
n.The Marches: The Marchers gained the chance to hunt the traitor Dalton Royse, to have their beaters paid to Beat the Bounds, and to build new fortifications. The first new Bounders Hall was commissioned in Bregasland.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's peerless kinship is said to have arisen from the flush of victory in Zenith.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland had no Imperial fortification, so an unbreakable, haunted fort at Fishers Rock with a Friar of the Dead Marshes was proposed. A Bounders Hall was commissioned there via a Wayleave to extend the beaters' protection.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was named as a possible site for a Bounders Hall and a Bailiff to extend the beaters' protection. Jotun ghosts also appeared at a farm in Oddmire.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold was under Jotun invasion and lost Bounders Hall, halting plans for paid beaters to Beat the Bounds until it is retaken. The Third Pie fortification was proposed to make it impossible to put the territory under threat.
t.Upwold: Upwold was named as a possible site for a Bounders Hall and a new Bailiff, so that the beaters could defend it against invasion.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the victory in Zenith is cited as the origin of Highguard's peerless kinship.

r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Spectral Jotun raiders gathered at Halebale Farm after farmers dug up an ancient relic, and locals insisted the Champion of Prosperity lead fighters and exorcists to clear them out.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Mentioned in passing: Freemoor's existing keep is one of the established fortresses the Third Pie would complete the Mourn's line of defences with.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: Greensward's existing keep is one of the established fortresses the Third Pie would complete the Mourn's line of defences with.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Much of Southmoor was held by Jotun armies, with hidden supply caches, the traitor Dalton Royse at large and Bounders Hall in Sarcombe fallen. The Third Pie fortification could be built at Sarcombe once the Jotun are driven out.

Last rays of the sun.d: In Miaren the Quiet Step stormed Rhonwen's Fall and killed the Empty Hands' Grand Archon. More than a hundred Navarr died, and both steadings and much ancient artwork were ruined. In Kronemark the Silence Arc used the Tower of the Eagle regio to build a mithril, crystal and ilium gate to bring more scions from Day. The Imperial assault killed the Grand Archon before the gate was anchored, and its collapse annihilated the scions. Over two hundred Imperial soldiers fell. A burning Sungate remains, held shut only while the Conclave keeps enmity with Cold Sun. Remnant scions now threaten Wood Heath, the Tower of Light and Shadow and the Icy Crag.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: some Navarr from Rhonwen's Fall fled into Astolat, and the pillar of fire was seen as far east as Laroc.
n.Highguard: Asenath led the Granite Pillar into Hahnmark and spearheaded the assault on the Tower of the Eagle, while Highborn warbands also fought in Miaren; Highborn soldiers were among those killed or marked by the collapsing gate.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm and the newly mustered Autumn Hammers protected the Highborn advance at the Tower of the Eagle, chanting the names of those lost in Skarsind; heralds of Janon and observers from the City of Bar and Bond accompanied them, and many orcs died or were scarred by the gate's backlash.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step's general urged the thorns on with the words "Liathaven awaits".
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step avenged the burning of First Voice Glade by destroying the Empty Hands, but more than a hundred Navarr were slain and the sanctuary and scholarship of Rhonwen's Fall were left in ruins.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the earlier beacon built in Segura with Lashonar's help is recalled as one of the victories against the scions.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the column of blue-green flame from the Tower of the Eagle was visible as far south as Tassato.
n.Urizen: Urizen warbands swelled the ranks fighting in Miaren, and a remnant scion force is advancing on the Tower of Light and Shadow in Redoubt, which the Penumbral Watcher Izora Highwind must stop.
n.Varushka: The Quiet Step marched out of Karov to fight in Miaren, and a scion remnant threatens to break the high hill above Volchitrava and damage the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun in Miekarova.
n.Wintermark: After six months of defending Hahnmark alone by the light of the beacons, Wintermark saw the Silence Arc destroyed, but it is left with a deadly Sungate in Kronemark and a scion threat to Wood Heath.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: some of the Navarr who lived at Rhonwen's Fall escaped into Astolat ahead of the scions.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the previous season's blunting of the Winnowers' dying curse in Bastion, aided by Lord Rain, is recalled.
t.Hahnmark: Three Imperial armies, independent warriors and the host of the red bear destroyed the Silence Arc at the Tower of the Eagle, but its ruins now hold a burning gate that kills anyone who comes within about a quarter mile.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step marched from Karov, and the earlier defence of the Haamrikoht Stone and events at Duzekani are recalled.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: named in the Quiet Step general's rallying cry, "Liathaven awaits".
t.Miaren: The Empty Hands were destroyed and their tree-killing aura ceased, but more than a hundred Navarr died, Rhonwen's Fall was ruined and a few scion warbands remain at large.
t.Miekarova: A remnant of the Blade of Skies threatens to break the hill above Volchitrava and damage the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun; Ceinwen Eternal, the Master of Ice and Darkness, must stop them and has received aid from Silverbrow.
t.Redoubt: Scions who looted the Brilliant Star are advancing on the Tower of Light and Shadow to transform it, and the Penumbral Watcher Izora Highwind is responsible for stopping them.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the beacon that artists and musicians built there with Lashonar to lure scion warbands is recalled.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the costly fight against the Still Walkers there, whose remnants unleashed storms across the territory, is recalled as the source of the orcs' grief.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the pillar of blue-green fire from Hahnmark could be seen from Tassato.

r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: The Silence Arc were destroyed at the Tower of the Eagle, and Kronemark now holds the Sungate, a lethal gateway to the Day realm kept closed only by Conclave enmity towards Cold Sun.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Scions are trying to unleash a disaster from a north-eastern peak that would devastate New Dunhall and nearby commissions, and Tobrytan Dunning, thane of Dunhearth Hall, must stop them.
r.Karov/Duzekani: Mentioned in passing: the events at the White Tower in Duzekani are recalled as a warning when planning the attack on the Tower of the Eagle.
r.Miaren/Greenfalls: The Empty Hands, based in Greenfalls, were annihilated at Rhonwen's Fall, but the Fallshome and Longshadow steadings were utterly ruined and the ancient carvings partly defaced.
r.Miaren/Serenael: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step entered Miaren at Serenael before moving south against the Empty Hands.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Mentioned in passing: the scions' earlier channelling of Storm Pass above Pakaanan's Pass, which damaged Whitelake, is recalled as the model for the threat to Wood Heath.

Less welcome tenants.d: Lutomysla learned that the Sand Fishers of Misericorde propitiate Dho'uala with seasonal offerings. She proposed three non-competing commissions: the Semmerlak Tollbooth, paying tribute of 30 Thrones a season; the Blades of the Semmerlak, a Dawnish knightly estate and Varushkan wardenhouse with a Knight-Warden title; and the Journeymage Towers for volhov, guisers and mountebanks, with a Watcher of the Semmerlak title. The Silent Bell suggested mandates for the Prosperity, Pride and Wisdom assemblies. Further options included later plenipotentiary diplomacy with Dho'uala over ilium and fishing, seeking the Lady of the Semmerlak's patronage, and a radical, costly idea of draining the lake. The Silent Bell also planned to publish its reports. All these opportunities have since expired.

n.Dawn: Many Dawnish, echoing Earl Ailsa Temerlaine, rejected propitiation and human sacrifice, and Dawnish knights, enchanters and guisers were central to two proposals: a knightly estate for the Blades of the Semmerlak and a role alongside the volhov in the Journeymage Towers.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj had tolerated the Sand Fishers' lake ceremonies so they could use them to bargain with Undertow, and their cruelty is contrasted with that of the Iron Helms.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: priests in Highguard were among those significantly concerned about proposals to sacrifice people to Dho'uala.
n.The League: Holberg's Waterroad Ring of merchant guilds, hurt by Dho'uala's attacks, backed the tribute idea if the Prosperity assembly declared it virtuous, while Holberg's mountebanks joined the volhov and League merchant-princes offered Goldentide Mail to a Knight-Warden.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen members of the Silent Bell objected that its secret letters smacked of conspiracy, pushing the sodality to share its reports publicly.
n.Varushka: Varushkan expertise underpinned the proposals: warden fellowships from Karov, Karsk and Ossium would staff a wardenhouse, the Wavewatcher volhov would lead the Journeymage Towers, and Varushkan merchant-boyars would supply magic items and could contribute to construction.

t.Holberg: Holberg's senator co-sponsored the appraisal, and its Sand Fisher region of Misericorde, the only part touching the lake, was offered as a Tollbooth site, while its merchants and mountebanks were key to the tribute and Journeymage proposals.
t.Karov: Warden fellowships from Karov helped shape the proposals, and the port of Korotny in Malimorzi was suggested for both a wardenhouse and a Journeymage Tower.
t.Karsk: Warden fellowships from Karsk took part in the talks, and as a lakeside territory Karsk could host the Tollbooth and would send representatives to any future talks with Dho'uala.
t.Ossium: Ossium's wardens contributed to the proposals, and the Kostjyas Respite in Bittershore was suggested as a site for a wardenhouse or a Journeymage Tower.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's senator Amicia of the Semmerlak co-sponsored the appraisal, its enchanters advised Lutomysla, and Lacuve near the port of Lacre was proposed for a knightly estate or a Journeymage Tower.
t.The Semmerlak: The lake is Dho'uala's domain, and every proposal aimed to stop her creatures preying on its shipping and shores, while a radical last-minute idea suggested draining it entirely to kill the sovereign.
t.Weirwater: Enchanters from Weirwater advised Lutomysla, and Sandling near Culwich was proposed as a possible site for the Dawnish knights' estate under the Blades of the Semmerlak.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Lutomysla visited the Sand Fishers' port here and learned of Reedpiper's offerings to Dho'uala; the orcs agreed the Empire could build the Tollbooth here, though they could withdraw access at will.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: The port of Korotny in Malimorzi was proposed as the site of both the Varushkan wardenhouse for the Blades of the Semmerlak and one of the Journeymage Towers.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The Kostjyas Respite in Bittershore was proposed as an alternative wardenhouse site and as one of the three Journeymage Tower locations.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Lacuve, near the port of Lacre, was proposed as a site for the Dawnish knightly estate, and Lacre itself for a Journeymage Tower, given that guisers are drawn to its tourneys and fairs.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Sandling, near Culwich, was put forward as one of two possible sites for the Dawnish knightly estate of the Blades of the Semmerlak.

Metal and stone.d: The Archmage of Autumn sent the Architects to three seats. For the Brilliant Star, Izenbra offered two ideas: bespoke tempest-jade ushabti from the Crucible of Fate, adding 3 wains of mithril a season, and the Tower of Shield and Spear to guard the mine. For the Vigilant Swan, Assessor Hedymarr offered swan-shaped construct guardians from the Manse of the Lionsmith, or a House of Fire and Flame expansion adding 4 wains of white granite that would destroy the Seminary of the Swan. For the Pride of Ikka's Tears, Architect Noether proposed the Bastion of the North fortification, which Estavus's heralds could build faster, and a deep shaft adding 5 wains of mithril. These are offers only, and the guild offers lapse after the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: they are blamed for turning the once-beautiful Vigilant Swan into a vast open-cast quarry worked by enslaved Highborn during their occupation of Reikos.
n.Grendel: Izenbra judged the Grendel of the Broken Shore the greatest threat to the Brilliant Star. A landing at Naris could let raiders strike the mine, its mithril caravans or the new skyways.
n.Highguard: Highborn face a hard choice at the Vigilant Swan. They could gain seven swan guardians, one for each virtue, or expand the quarry at the cost of the Seminary of the Swan, which local Highborn already mourn as a reminder of the Druj occupation.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: invasion from Jotun is cited as one of the dangers that make fortifying the Pride of Ikka's Tears worthwhile.
n.Thule: Threats from Thule and a continuing breakdown in relations with the orcs of Otkodov help justify the proposed Bastion of the North. Negotiation with the Thule of the Silver Peaks is suggested as one possible route for mithril caravans.
n.Urizen: Urizen is offered ways to strengthen the Brilliant Star. The Architect of the Crucible could turn the Crucible's ushabti to mining, and the Tower of Shield and Spear, garrisoned by Redoubt's sentinels, could secure the mine's mithril.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Pride of Ikka's Tears could gain a great fortification to rival Kalant and Olgafsdottirshal, with a garrison drawn from Sermersuaq's warriors. A deep shaft could also make it one of the Empire's most lucrative mithril mines.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed, and the link appears to come only from the name of the proposed Bastion of the North fortification in Sermersuaq.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: holding Sermersuaq regions that link to Hahnmark is named as the easiest way to keep mithril flowing from the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: a continuing breakdown in relations with the orcs of Otkodov is cited as one reason for urgency in fortifying the Sermersuaq mine.
t.Redoubt: The Brilliant Star beneath Tomari could gain mithril-mining ushabti and a sentinel-held tower to protect its output. Izenbra privately admitted that its help there would be limited.
t.Reikos: The Vigilant Swan could gain construct guardians or a major expansion of white granite. The expansion would drain the lakes and destroy the Seminary of the Swan.
t.Sermersuaq: The Pride of Ikka's Tears could be ringed by the Bastion of the North and deepened with a new shaft. Both would boost mithril output and shield the mine from barbarians and monsters.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: attacks by creatures out of Tsirku are listed among the threats to the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
t.Zenith: The Crucible of Fate in Zenith could switch its bespoke ushabti from supporting Zenith's restoration to working the Brilliant Star, and its koboldi are eager to help design them.

r.Redoubt/Naris: Mentioned in passing: Naris is named as the likely landing point for a Grendel force that might raid the Brilliant Star or its caravans.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Tomari, home of the Brilliant Star, is the proposed site of the Tower of Shield and Spear. The mine would hold out with the tower's sentinels unless the whole region fell.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: Riverwatch could be guarded by seven swan constructs that fight only within the region. Its lakes and the Seminary of the Swan would be lost if the quarry were widened.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: negotiation with the Thule of the Silver Peaks is suggested as one alternative route for getting mithril out of Sermersuaq.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Suaq Fount is the proposed site of both the Bastion of the North, a rank two fortification, and the deep shaft that would add 5 wains of mithril a season.

Only forward.d: The Fist of Ulven, led by Gjeirfund Haggarsdottir rather than King Gudmunder, advanced cautiously, fearing Night wards, while Bjorgthorn Hammerhand's Southern Bear pressed boldly. They met only levies and a few absent Strong Reeds. Graven Rock fell at once, again denying the Keeper of the Dour Fens its mana, and the Jotun began fortifying it. The Jotun's caution gave the rest of Bregasland time to prepare. A battle opportunity followed: stop Adamant's Mountain Bulwark from restoring the Burhfæst fortification, capture the ghodi Svynna to ransom four Navarr thralls, and show Pride at the Graven Door to lift Bregasland's sullen mood. A Jotun warband under Urse Longarm also raided Mitwold.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun call the Navarr "Imperial Druj" as they execute them at Graven.
n.Jotun: Jotun armies seized Gravenmarch and began fortifying Graven Rock, and Adamant has offered them the Burhfæst fortification for a year. The Ice Fishers of Ldansk and the Howling Bears joined the campaign, and Urse Longarm's warband raided Mitwold.
n.Navarr: Two Navarr stridings caught in Graven fought beside the Marchers, and the Jotun executed every Navarr survivor in revenge for past dishonour. The exception was the Graven Stand family of four, taken as thralls by Svynna of Ldansk, who might be ransomed if the ghodi is captured.
n.The Marches: The Marchers lost Gravenmarch, and those captured were offered the Choice. The Bregas yeomen are arming and waiting for the Strong Reeds to return, and a show of Pride at the Graven Door offers a chance to restore the region's morale.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is not named; the only northern link is the Ice Fishers of Ldansk, drawn from minor clans across Kalsea who fight for Kierheim and Tromsa.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland lost Gravenmarch to the Jotun, and the Keeper of the Dour Fens lost its mana bounty for the second time in a year. The rest of the territory is preparing to resist while a lingering sullen mood persists.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the captured Navarr family may be destined for thralldom further west in Hordalant.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun, who now call it Ashvale, launched the invasion of Gravenmarch from Liathaven. Svynna's captive Navarr were taken there, and Urse Longarm had earlier won a victory there against a Feni enclave.
t.Mitwold: Urse Longarm's warband raided Mitwold's farmland and roads, evading the scattered Strong Reeds. The Bailiff of the Grand Market, Sebastian Shaw, is charged with killing them before their fame draws more Jotun raiders.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is not named on the page; the only northern reference is to the Ice Fishers of Ldansk and the lands of Kalsea.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the Ice Fishers of Ldansk are said to fight for the honour of Kierheim, Tromsa and more distant lands.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch fell to the Jotun, who took Graven Rock and the town of Graven and are fortifying the plateau. The battle opportunity centres here, at Graven Rock and the Graven Door near Rock Foot Wood.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Mentioned in passing: the sullen mood affecting the Grey Fens could be dispelled by a show of Pride at the Graven Door if the Strong Reeds return.

Peaks and planes.d: Following Clytemnestra's and Jedediah Boon's statements, the Urizen Assembly could send mages, sentinels and sword scholars to help bring in the Marcher harvest, raising every Marcher farm's income but halving the Doyen of the Spires' research. Elagabala's alternative would also push Urizen armies to support the Tusks and Strong Reeds against Jotun. The Marcher Assembly could send friars to Urizen, boosting Urizen congregations at a cost to Marcher ones, or back Rhubarb Ironwood's more confrontational version. The Assembly's and Emperor Vesna's denunciations of those praising the condemned covens instead drove more Marchers to support them. Jack Tiller, Frankie Moulder and Old Tam Witch-hazel were coming to Anvil to talk it out.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Elagabala's proposed alternate mandate speaks of Urizen helping defend the Marches from Jotun incursion.
n.The Marches: The Marches might gain Urizeni harvest helpers and could send friars to Urizen at a cost to its own congregations, while its people grew openly at odds with their Assembly over its condemnation of the cursing covens and its failure to see sorcerers punished.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Assembly could send its mages, sentinels and sword scholars to labour on Marcher farms at the cost of halving the Doyen of the Spires' research, and its congregations would gain from any visiting Marcher friars.

t.Bregasland: Under Elagabala's proposed alternate mandate, Urizen military units would be encouraged to support the Strong Reeds defending Bregasland, with any that did not losing strength as warriors went to the Marches instead.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Old Tam Witch-hazel, a Mitwold landskeeper, was persuaded to travel to Anvil to speak with the shunned covens.
t.Mournwold: The past cursing of the Mournwold, which killed thousands of Marchers, fuels the present distrust of magic, and Elagabala's proposed mandate would encourage Urizen forces to support the Tusks in the Mournwold.

r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: Jedediah Boon is named as being of the Ore Hills, his pride in his land having inspired Clytemnestra's pilgrimage.

Pitter patter.d: After the Chamber of Commerce chose to ride out the plague, bites spread a hallucinatory sickness that was treatable with bladeroot and, in bad cases, prismatic ink. The Unfettered Mind, protected by League captains, found about one rat in twelve enchanted, the source beneath the city, and wolf-sized rats in the tunnels. Rituals identified the domain of the King of Rats. Brinton von Temeschwar offered to sell a token for safe contact, and the Rat Kings guild sought talks with the Chamber, which again faced a vote. At Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, tainted air left nearly a third of workers ill, reducing the Delver of the Depths' bounty.

n.The League: League captains guarded the investigating magicians, and League magicians confirmed Shadowsmith's fate. Temeschwar's business owners again had to choose between the Wardog Kennels, the Guild of the Green Flower, possibly the Rat Kings, or riding out the plague.
n.Varushka: Varushkans built the city in pre-Imperial times. A coven of Varushkan cabalists proved a Winter ward against the swarms possible but ruinously costly, and sensed a powerful, malign force ruling parts of the undercity.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a Steinr runesmith helped treat the stricken Cartagia, a Wintermark magician was mauled by a giant rat, and the Steinr grimnir Kylara is a voting member of the Chamber of Commerce.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a Holberg scholar's pet rats stayed placid in Temeschwar, suggesting only the city's own rats are affected, and Albrecht Von Holberg was among the rat hunters.
t.Temeschwar: Rat swarms, a spreading sickness and a sovereign-like King of Rats beneath the city disrupted daily life. Those who could fled, physicks were kept busy, and the mine at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets lost workers to tainted air and disappearances.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: A Sentinel Gate conjunction opened to the Old Priory inn in Temeschwar, Hanuri, where Brinton von Temeschwar offered to sell a token allowing safe contact with the King of Rats.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Mentioned in passing: a 'fell wind' blowing in off the Vardstein Vale preceded the sickness among workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Poetry and prose.d: Three proposals were made for the Towers of Dawn site at Dawnguard: Etienne de Maravel's Tombs of Glory, Christian's Gates of Adventure with a Knight of the Gate, and Josephine du Lune's Towers of Enchantment college, two of whose four eternal patrons are under enmity. A mandate could consecrate the remodelled Spires of Dusk to Ambition, raising Dawn's army capacity. A folly at Hope's Rest could spread Dawnish settlement. The Rahvin mourned the vetoed treaty and armed themselves with some Black Wind at the Fangs. Most Navarr swore the Loyalty-backed oath to protect the Great Forest Orcs, who are now fleeing the Druj in Therunin. Legal advice held the treaty may not have been broken.

n.Dawn: Dawn could choose between three ambitious rebuilds of the Towers of Dawn, a consecration of the Spires of Dusk that would let it support an extra army, and a chapel at Hope's Rest to spur new Dawnish settlement, though its people were warned to keep away from the Great Forest Orcs.
n.Druj: The Druj saw the last traces of their power stripped from the Spires of Dusk, faced the prospect of a Dawnish surge aimed at their surrounding territories, and invaded Therunin, overwhelming the Great Forest Orcs there.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Etienne de Maravel studied sculpture in Necropolis under the Highborn artist Dinah of Sanctuary's End, and the Highborn tombs for dead Thrones inspired her Tombs of Glory.
n.Navarr: Driven by Brynn Tendfallen's mandate and the Loyalty Assembly's use of the Eyes of Loyalty, most Navarr swore a binding oath to protect the Great Forest Orcs as family, and Chief Vallack's party planned to meet them at Anvil.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Josephine du Lune cited the Brass Coast's Lyceum, still hidden in its misty wards, as an example of a national college of magic Dawn lacks.
n.The League: A League citizen, Serrusto Caeli Rezia di Tassato, raised the call to consecrate the Spires of Dusk, whose remodelling had been paid for by the Castellan of Spiral Castle.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Doyen of the Spires was cited as an example of a national college of magic Dawn lacks.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Icy Crag was cited as an example of a college of magic, and Varushkans were warned to keep their distance from the visiting Great Forest Orcs.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Tombs of Glory were likened to the Wintermark Chronicle of Heroes.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Druj territories the Dawnish would set their sights on if the Spires of Dusk were consecrated to Ambition.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Etienne de Maravel is said to have studied architecture in Holberg.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Lyceum, the Brass Coast's college of magic still hidden by misty wards, was cited by Josephine du Lune.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the Icy Crag was cited as Varushka's college of magic.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Etienne de Maravel studied sculpture here, and she found that Rodric the Lame has no tomb of his own in the Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: recalled as a land from which the Dawnish drove the Druj.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Druj territories the Dawnish would set their sights on if the Spires of Dusk were consecrated to Ambition.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the Druj territories the Dawnish would set their sights on if the Spires of Dusk were consecrated to Ambition.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle paid for the remodelling of the Spires of Dusk.
t.The Barrens: Now firmly Dawnish, the Barrens faced proposals to rebuild the Towers of Dawn, consecrate the Spires of Dusk and expand Dawnish settlement, while most Black Wind departed and the Rahvin armed themselves at the Fangs.
t.Therunin: The Druj invaded Therunin, overwhelming the Great Forest Orc warriors who had tried to delay them and who were now falling back from steadings near the Holt of the Oak and the Thimble.

r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The ruins of the Towers of Dawn here could become the Tombs of Glory, the Gates of Adventure or the Towers of Enchantment college of magic, depending on which proposal the Empire chose.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Shrine of Hope, now holding a true aura of Ambition and haunted by Ser Guineve, could gain a chapel folly to turn a trickle of visitors into a flood and spread Dawnish settlement.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Murderdale was named as unclaimed land that new Dawnish houses would settle if a chapel were built at the Shrine of Hope.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Parts of the Bleaks not claimed by the Karass were named as land the Dawnish would settle if a chapel were built at the Shrine of Hope.

Rebuild Drycastle.d: Proposed by the Senator for the Barrens and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion commissioned repairs to Drycastle following the 'A glorious victory' Wind of Fortune. It cost 20 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns, and 50 thrones were disbursed to the Senator for the Barrens. Many citizens donated materials and money between Summer 386YE and Spring 387YE, and the work was completed. The Knight of Dawnguard, chosen by unanimous decision of the Dawnish senators, guards the region and its settlements. The Reeve of Drycastle, held by a yeofolk and chosen by Tally of the Votes of Dawnish military captains, oversees the town's prosperity. Both titles became available from Summer Solstice 387YE.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained a rebuilt Drycastle and two new Dawnish titles: the Knight of Dawnguard, chosen unanimously by Dawn's senators, and the Reeve of Drycastle, a yeofolk chosen by Tally of the Votes from Summer 387YE.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the motion describes liberated citizens living in the ashes and rubble left by the Druj.

t.The Barrens: The town of Drycastle in Dawnguard was rebuilt from the ruins left by the Druj, and the Barrens now has a Knight charged with securing Dawnguard and a Reeve overseeing Drycastle's prosperity.

Rebuild the Storm Vault.d: Tiberius Echostorm, Crystal Architect of the Spires, announced the rebuilding of the Storm Vault, a mana sinecure in Proceris that had been sacked by the Druj. The work cost 8 wains of mithril and 10 thrones and took three months; the materials and money were provided by Xanthius Storm's End after the Summer Solstice 386YE. Once complete, the Custodian of the Storm Vault again received 10 mana crystals each season and could fund the gathering of precious tempest jade through a ministry.

n.Druj: The Druj had sacked the Storm Vault and left it infested, and this rebuilding undid that damage.
n.Urizen: Urizeni leaders announced and paid for the rebuilding, which restored a valuable mana sinecure and a tempest jade ministry to the nation.

t.Zenith: The Storm Vault in Zenith was rebuilt from its sacked, infested state and once again produced mana crystals for its custodian.

r.Zenith/Proceris: The Storm Vault in Proceris was repaired over three months, and its custodian again received 10 mana crystals each season and could fund the gathering of tempest jade.

Repair Capodomus Cathedral.d: Announced by Estella Lucati di Sarvos as proxy to the Master of Rings, the commission followed the Old Ways Wind of Fortune. It cost 20 white granite, 10 mithril and 90 crowns and took three months. Jules von Holberg, Estella Lucati, Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos, Sebastiano and Luciana Valesi each gave mithril, white granite and money, and Gino de Sarvos, Luca Lucati and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg added further coin. The motion hoped to restore the oldest and greatest cathedral to the Way of Virtue and ready it for consecration with True Liao as a symbol of rebirth. The work is complete, and the National Assembly may now appoint the Archbishop each Summer Solstice.

n.The League: The League National Assembly gained the annual appointment of the Archbishop of Capodomus, who coordinates and supports the Assembly and acts as a point of contact. League citizens largely funded the repairs.

t.Sarvos: The Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos was finally restored after the Grendel sack and made ready for consecration with True Liao, intended as a symbol of the city's rebirth and renewal.

Repair the Sapphire Stair.d: The Sapphire Stair was damaged by Eisa Winterborn during the raid described in the Shallows and Miseries Wind of War. The Senate authorised its repair at the cost set out in the opportunity: 10 wains each of white granite, weirwood and mithril, plus 90 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice 386YE, Raphael Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato supplied 10 wains each of mithril, weirwood and white granite, along with 11 thrones and 2 crowns. With the work finished, the Keeper of the Sapphire Stair once again receives their previous income.

n.The League: A League landmark damaged in a hostile raid was restored, largely funded and supplied by the League citizen Raphael Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato, and its Keeper's income was restored.

t.Tassato: The Sapphire Stair in Tassato, damaged in Eisa Winterborn's raid, was rebuilt on the motion of Tassato's own senator, and its Keeper now receives their former income again.

Rock and a hard place.d: The Westmere Council asked the Senator for Mitwold what to do with the cursed rune-carved stone, and the Senator ordered it brought to Anvil. The Conclave instead declared it should go to Estavus. Heralds of the Prince of Shikal reclaimed it, and the herald Calabris declared the deal void. The smiths who had served Estavus since before the Empire were therefore released. The landskeeper Hester led them back via the Woldstone in Ashbrook to Oakwood Monastery. They were unaged but confused, remembering little but their craft. Aliss Thorn's Synod mandate passed by a greater majority (244-0), sending artisans to Oakwood. As a result, the smith archetype will join the Marcher archetypes after the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the drovers carrying the stone had taken the road from King's Stoke toward Navarr-held Miaren when their wagon broke.
n.The Marches: The Marches regained scores of smiths lost to Estavus for centuries, along with their lost art of hammer, flame and bargaining with the small folk. The Assembly's mandate means the smith archetype will be added to the Marcher archetypes after the Autumn Equinox.

t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the wagon carrying the stone broke on the direct route from King's Stoke toward Miaren, where the heralds dismantled it.
t.Upwold: The freed smiths reappeared at the Woldstone in Upwold. They were taken in by Oakwood Monastery, where artisans from across the Marches gathered to help them recover and to learn from them.

r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Hester returned at the Woldstone in Ashbrook leading a column of bemused smiths. From there they headed to the nearby Oakwood Monastery to seek the monks' help.

Set my lands in order.d: Orcs of Skarsind, led by the Sannite sept, began moving to Mareave along trods extended by Navarr. The first Senator for Mareave was to be elected at the Summer Solstice for a nine-month term, by voters not eligible in Skarsind's last election. Salt-Lord Ehsan's Beoraidh will send the senator 10 crowns a season in gifts. Icarion is under-developed; Icarion, Nadir and Eoradal are arid; Clisearn, Eoradal and Fleisardh are uncooperative; Fleisardh is under threat; and the only land route runs through Spiral. The Assembly may each season send a different sept to Mareave. Ehsan offers mazzarine for dragonbone and poor land for a shrine. The Senate may allocate the Fundindelve mine, and Regrow the Land's Heart had little effect.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is cited as a comparable territory whose integration takes a year or more.
n.Grendel: The Grendel are expected to try to reclaim Mareave, which they regard as part of the Broken Shore, and the Brine Turtles of Fleisardh still support an army in their service.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation now holds two territories and will elect its first Senator for Mareave. It faces aridity, under-development, hostile southern orcs and a Grendel threat, and its Assembly can send a different sept each season to help settle the land.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Voice of the Quiet Forest extended the trods into Mareave, easing the orcs' journey south.
n.The Brass Coast: With its experience of dry plains, the Brass Coast is suggested as a nation whose Assembly could offer expertise to help reclaim Mareave's arid regions.
n.The League: The League, especially its Apulian orcs, is suggested as a source of help with moving materials into under-developed Mareave. Ehsan's opening haggle over shrine land is a move the League would recognise.
n.The Marches: As the Empire's acknowledged masters of agriculture, the Marchers are suggested as able to help grow crops in Mareave's near-desertified regions if their Assembly asks.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as a comparable territory whose challenges take a long time to resolve.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: some orcs of southern Mareave fled south into Ayereed after the conquest.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the treaty with Beoraidh guarantees Imperial access to the bay, albeit with tariffs, though this does not help move armies.
t.Mareave: Newly assigned to the Imperial Orcs, Mareave gains its first senatorial election and settlers, but suffers arid, under-developed, uncooperative and threatened regions, cannot support an Imperial army, and remains a likely target for Grendel reconquest.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as a precedent for regional qualities that represent the challenges of settling a territory.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a rebuilt Eoradal aqueduct is likened to the Colossus of Sarvos as a possible wonder.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: even Segura is said to have more water than Mareave.
t.Skarsind: Many orcs of Skarsind, especially Sannites, debated or began leaving for Mareave, while others stayed. Those eligible to vote for Skarsind's senator last winter cannot vote for Mareave's.
t.Spiral: The Apulian Way through Spiral is the only land route to Mareave, risking passage near the Black Plateau, and Spiral's inhabitants have first-hand experience of Ehsan's city-state.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Retained by Ehsan's city-state under treaty, Beoraidh holds the territory's only real port. Its factions will send gifts to the new senator, and Ehsan offered a meagre plot in its worst quarter for a shrine of the Way.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn is uncooperative, its remaining wealthy Grendel and skilled miners resentful. It is open to assault from the south, and its mountains hold Fundindelve, a mithril mine producing 22 wains a season that awaits allocation by the Senate.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal is both arid and uncooperative, with hostile Brine Turtles and former Grendel servants. The ruins of an immense Skouran aqueduct there could perhaps be rebuilt as a wonder.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Home of the Brine Turtles, who still back a Grendel army, Fleisardh is uncooperative and under threat as a gateway for any Grendel return.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Icarion is under-developed and arid, raising commission labour costs and harming farms across Mareave, though its scattered orcs are cautiously interested in the Imperial Orcs.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Nadir is arid and sparsely settled, mostly by mining communities, but its orcs, many linked to the Sannite sept, are cautiously open to Imperial Orc rule.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Kept by Beoraidh under the treaty, Sinfoyard's herb gardens supply the cerulean mazzarine Ehsan offers in trade for dragonbone. Its inhabitants are among those courting the new senator with gifts.

Standards.d: Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir's Lion of the North, reinforced by Tromsan siege engineers, joined Derun Stonetower's Tower of the North. Jarl Haakon's warband and Stephen of Sarcombe's yegarra fought alongside them. Captured Marchers, orcs included, were offered the Choice, and those who refused became thralls. Rumour says Haakon condemned the yegarra's dishonourable conduct and Yrsa made Stephen swear to uphold Jotun honour or be cast out. Nearly ten thousand orcs overwhelmed about six thousand defenders at Sarcombe, which had no fortress. The Imperial positions and ministries tied to Sarcombe were lost. The people expect the Tusks to return by the Autumn Equinox. Jotun ghosts were also sighted near the Liathaven border.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named only to suggest the Jotun are unlikely to harm the Sarcombe Register, since they are not the Druj.
n.Jotun: Two Jotun armies led by Queen Yrsa and Derun Stonetower, aided by Jarl Haakon and Stephen of Sarcombe's yegarra, retook much of Southmoor and raised their standards over Sarcombe. Rumours also told of friction between Haakon and Stephen over the yegarra's conduct.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are suggested as possible helpers in investigating the Jotun ghosts, since the orcs currently hold Liathaven.
