n.The Marches: The Marches lost three-fifths of Southmoor and the market town of Sarcombe, along with the ministries, offices and incomes tied to it. Marcher orcs who refused the Choice were made thralls again, and the folk of the Mourn now expect the Tusks to return by the Autumn Equinox.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Jotun armies were marching into Bregasland at the same time, and some of the Fisher household, their ambitions there shattered, now fought under Stephen of Sarcombe.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun-held forests served as the launching point for the invasion of Southmoor. A haunt of Jotun ghosts was sighted on its border with the Mournwold.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun returned to the Mourn, seizing most of Southmoor and Sarcombe and once again forcing the Choice on its people.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Olgafsdottir of Tromsa sent siege engineers south to bolster Queen Yrsa's army.

r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: The Jotun force moved east out of Liaven's Glen to begin the invasion, and the Jotun ghosts appeared to be heading towards the Glen of Red Shadow there.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: the defeated Imperial garrisons and some Southmoor folk made a fighting retreat towards the Greensward.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: the retreating Imperial soldiers and some Southmoor folk fell back towards the Ore Hills.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Three-fifths of Southmoor, including Sarcombe, fell after the town's gates were broken by siege engines. A beacon now burns where Hillstop once stood, Jotun standards fly over the Old Oak Inn, and those who stayed face the Choice. Jotun ghosts were also reported in the north of the region.

Tales of imagination.d: Barien let Imperial heroes reach the Four Corners Fair from the Imperial regio, and each nation's egregore received invitations for five people. Meraud asked Catrina Words of Dawn to help run a game there. Sanvar Isk feuded with the orphans of the Little Mother and would again auction the Loom of Spells. Cathan Canae's heralds defended the Kallavesa and Hahnmark beacons, and she pledged the Drums of the Iron Harpoon if beacons are built in Sermersuaq and a white bear statue is raised. Azoth judged that the Navarr had transformed their nation. Janon's Shadowed Torchbrand title became available to appoint. Sadogua made offers to the Lyceum and the Marcher landskeepers. Jaheris and Eleonaris arranged a debate in Foracci. Barien announced a Pinnacle Tourney, and Lashonar sought letters of longing.

n.Dawn: Meraud sent a special invitation to Catrina Words The Unbelievably Magical, asking her to help run a game at the Four Corners Fair. Dawn's enchanters are said to know the Fair well, and the Knight of Roses received the nation's five invitations.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel threat is cited as the reason the Lyceum's scholars remain hidden behind walls of mist.
n.Navarr: Azoth declared itself satisfied that the Navarr had made a profound, lasting change to their nation. It offered to help reattune the last singing stone for Navarr covens once the Archmage of Night arranges a parley. Liaven also received the nation's invitations to the Four Corners Fair.
n.The League: Tassato's playwrights and comedians gleefully satirised Sanvar Isk's feud with the orphans of the Little Mother. Jaheris and Eleonaris's debate contest was set for the Solare Estate in Sarvos, overseen by the Guerra arbiters, and Escon received the League's Fair invitations.
n.Urizen: Meraud's magical lion-owl delivered an invitation to Menos of Urizen allowing five Urizen to visit the Four Corners Fair.
n.Varushka: Jaheris's silver-tongued emissary brought Mother Varushka an invitation for five Varushkans to visit the Four Corners Fair. A herald of Lashonar would also hand out tokens near the Varushkan Fire.
n.Wintermark: Cathan Canae's warrior-heralds defended the beacons of Kallavesa and Hahnmark. She pledged a third ritual, the Drums of the Iron Harpoon, if Sermersuaq's beacons are built and a white granite bear statue honours her aid, and she means to give it to the general of the Narwhal's Spear. Sulkavaris received the nation's Fair invitations.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the last singing stone that Azoth offers to help reattune was recovered from the depths of Brocéliande.
t.Hahnmark: Crimson-robed bear-people of Cathan Canae emerged from Kalpaheim and fought alongside the Imperial armies there to defeat Cold Sun, defending the beacons.
t.Kallavesa: Wolf-like archers and scouts of Cathan Canae came forth from Rundahl Hall to protect the marshes and their beacons alongside Wintermark's heroes.
t.Miaren: A brightly painted herald of Azoth arrived in Seren with the eternal's message that it was ready to help the Navarr reattune the singing stone.
t.Sarvos: The Solare Estate in Sarvos was chosen to host the debate contest between the champions of Jaheris and Eleonaris. Eliza di Sarvos is also named as a past participant in a Lashonar opportunity.
t.Sermersuaq: Cathan Canae pledged that if beacons are built in Sermersuaq she will grant the Drums of the Iron Harpoon to call forth tusked-folk to protect them. In return she asks for a white granite bear statue on the shores of Lake Atkonaroq.
t.Tassato: Sanvar Isk's broadsheets and his commissioned play 'The Rats Of The Little Mother' became a comic sensation in Tassato. His attempt to sue the theatre company turned the play into a runaway commercial success.

r.Sarvos/Foracci: The Solare Estate in Foracci would host the debate between Jaheris's and Eleonaris's champions at 11pm on the Saturday of the Summer Solstice. The Sentinel Gate allows up to 100 people to attend.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: One of Cathan Canae's ogre-like heralds came to Atalaq bearing her pledge of a third boon if beacons are built in Sermersuaq.

Tales of mystery.d: The Deadwood Knight answered the Earl of Fools' challenge by sending over a hundred unliving warriors against the Earl's estate. Dawnish and Varushkan defenders repelled them. Brass Coast hakima who attended the Spring Equinox were cursed by the Three Sisters, and the Urizeni stargazer Cassius was returning to Anvil. Memory-swapping through Cast Off the Chain of Memory ceased, but tales spread of Night magicians losing their identities. An unseen beast began stalking Kalpaheim after Ogila's Tower cracked. Navarr reclaimed Miaren's calcified trees as art. Combing the Beach lost its power in exchange for Netweaver's Eye. A cambion whale harried ships in the Sea of Snow. Conjunctions were offered to Gorek's Reach and the Starstrand steading.

n.Dawn: The Earl of Fools' estate was attacked by the Deadwood Knight's unliving cohort, which left behind the heads of the troubadours Gerard and Margueritte of Valewatch. Separately, a Dawnish guiser gained a long-dead wizard's ritual knowledge through stolen memories and has since disappeared.
n.Navarr: Inspired by an enchantment and Nathair Autumngale's statement of principle, the Navarr turned Miaren's bone trees into living art, a practice stridings carried across the Empire. The Starstrand steading meanwhile sought Imperial help with a strange affliction.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: The Marches are not named on this page, and no event described takes place in Marcher lands.
n.Urizen: An Urizeni illuminate was among three Night magicians brought to the Quiet Hall with a fractured identity. The Urizeni stargazer Cassius was returning to Anvil with new portents concerning the Three Sisters.
n.Varushka: The Varushka assembly urged its soldiery to band together against the Schlacta of Rot, and Varushkan warriors helped repel the attack on the Earl of Fools' estate. Tales also spoke of two Varushkan cabalists who traded away their childhood memories, and of former cultists discovered in Moresvah.
n.Wintermark: A mysterious unseen beast began stalking Kalpaheim after Ogila's Tower cracked. A Wintermark mystic was also among the Night magicians left with a shattered identity by memory-swapping.

t.Brocéliande: The Starstrand steading in Boar's Dell, near the Semmerholm border, was afflicted by a feeling of incompleteness after a merrow offered to "call down the stars". Heroes were invited to investigate.
t.Hahnmark: In Kalpaheim, a roar from Ogila's Tower left a crack through its regio, and the sounds and breath of an unseen great beast began spreading across the city at night. Some rumours accused the tower's owner, Kaapo Kingfishering, of a dark pact.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesa is not named on this page, and none of its events take place there.
t.Karov: The Deadwood Knight continued to build its forces in Karov, threatening the people there, and it cannot yet be permanently destroyed.
t.Karsk: In the vale of Gorek's Reach in Karsk, the volhov Rakhel Vitkusovna discovered many adults were former cultists seeking to atone. The Custodian of the Lost was charged with finding out more.
t.Miaren: A Night enchantment charged Miaren with inspiration, and its people painted, carved and decorated the trees calcified by Cold Sun's Empty Hand, transforming them into works of art before the magic faded.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named on this page, and none of its events take place there.
t.Sea of Snow: A scarred cambion whale rammed ships and swallowed objects held overboard, favouring laden trading vessels. The Lictors believe a Callidus herald inside it is corrupting the creature, and its attacks may come to affect trade with Faraden.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the afflicted Starstrand steading sits almost on the border between Brocéliande and Semmerholm, so Dawn was asked to be represented among the volunteers.
t.Weirwater: The Deadwood Knight continued to build its unliving forces in Weirwater and remained a looming threat to its people.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is not named on this page; its only Urizeni links are the stargazer Cassius and an afflicted illuminate.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The Starstrand steading in Boar's Dell was the site of a conjunction for 50 participants. It was organised by the Spear of the Seven, Corwyn Heartsbane, to investigate an aura driving people to seek connection.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Mentioned in passing: West Marsh is not named on this page, and none of its events take place there.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The shunned vale of Gorek's Reach in Moresvah was found to be home to former cultists of an unknown power. A possible combat encounter there fell to the Custodian of the Lost, Anthemius Netherwatch.

The city below.d: Urizeni magicians, many aligned with the Deathless Cave, offered to help shape Apulian's character. The League Assembly enacted Lia Adelaar van Holberg's mandate urging Apulians to embrace them, backed by the Loyalty Assembly. Actius proposed the Chamber of Euphony, which could be ceded to Sung as a fane creating the title Map to the City Below; it remains open for commission until the 387YE Summer Solstice. Apulian orcs doubted the warned Grendel plot to weaponise the Black Plateau, and no public action was taken. Urizen's mandate released the Block's secrets, removing commission penalties in Spiral. The League condemned the Company of the Venturesome Harrier's Plateau tours as a scam. Blue Spring-touched flowers blossomed across Spiral.

n.Grendel: Imperial assemblies warned of a Grendel plot to weaponise the Black Plateau, but Apulian's orcs judged the nation to have neither the skill nor the will for it. Sharing the Block's secrets openly now leaves them within easy reach of Grendel spies.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the mausoleums of the Necropolis are cited as resonating with the Winter realm, by way of comparison with cities.
n.The League: The League Assembly enacted a mandate urging Apulians to learn from their Urizeni neighbours and condemned the Harrier company's Plateau tours as a scam. The League may also commission the Chamber of Euphony and a national Map to the City Below.
n.Urizen: Urizeni magicians of the Deathless Cave became a common sight in Apulian and offered to share their culture and Sung's patronage. The Urizen Assembly, by a greater majority but with notable dissent, chose to share the secrets of the Block with the League.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's grandeur and the City of Locks' regio in one of its clock towers are cited as comparisons for Apulian.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: its mausoleums are cited as an example of places resonating with the Winter realm.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Apulian is said to fall far short of Sarvos's size, and several Sarvosan figures appear in the related votes and tasks.
t.Spiral: Apulian's character began to absorb Urizeni philosophy and magic, and the Block's secrets removed the Black Plateau's penalty on commissions in the territory. Blue Spring-touched flowers bloomed across it, refreshing some people and making others violent.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's Varushkan heritage is cited as a model for Apulian, and a Temeschwar priest raised the statement condemning the Harrier tours.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra has returned to the Empire, and the Night mages of its Deathless Cave, now hidden behind Sung's mithril statues, have grown comfortable mixing with their League neighbours.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The rebellion in Cinion's mountains has been stabilised after the Senate recognised the Silver Flame there as foreigners, though reconciliation with Caeli's rebels remains distant.
r.Spiral/Screed: Two Harrier hiking parties ran into trouble in the woods of Screed near the Black Plateau, with Estella Lucati and the Mistress of Medicine asked to rescue them.

The final countdown.d: Statements by Aniera of Exiles End, Siân Eternal and Doctor Lysimachus stirred hopes of finally ending the vallorn, though some urged caution. The Navarr Assembly could mandate either total commitment or a decade of preparation. Failing to choose by the end of the Autumn Equinox would have caused a catastrophic loss of confidence. The Highborn Assembly could recall the grey pilgrims, and other nations could issue statements of principle. The war would begin once trods were cast in Béantal Dol in Sarangrave and in Kabanja and Visokuma in Axos. The Navarr committed in Summer, with most stridings leaving the trods and their armies rising from three to six. Highguard followed in Autumn, raising its armies from three to four.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Siân Eternal cites Dawn's questing knights, alongside the grey pilgrims, as having joined the Navarr cause to eradicate the vallorn.
n.Druj: The Druj had just invaded Therunin. It was argued that triggering the vallorn heart in the Sarangrave would spell disaster for them, forcing them to pull back armies to contain it. The Navarr must also time their trod castings so the Druj cannot take them down.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are noted as not yet defeated in the South, and Doctor Lysimachus warns Highguard to prepare for them on its shores.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly chose in Autumn 386YE to commit to the war against the vallorn. The grey pilgrims stopped walking the trods and returned home, and the armies Highguard can support rose from three to four.
n.Jotun: The Jotun, already attacking in the West and holding Liathaven, were cited as likely to be forced to divert armies if the Liathaven vallorn burst forth from its heart.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly committed the entire nation to the war against the vallorn in Summer 386YE. Most stridings stopped walking the trods and returned home, and the armies the Navarr can maintain rose from three to six.

t.Bastion: A Highborn commitment to the vallorn war raised the question of whether to keep building the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion while the Empire's survival might be at stake.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: it is recalled as the place where a rare chance to weaken a vulnerable vallorn was lost because 'it was not the time'.
t.Liathaven: Recalled as Navarr land lost to the Jotun, with its steadings destroyed. Triggering its vallorn heart was argued to be a way to force the Jotun to divert armies against westward vallorn expansion.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named on the page; it is linked only as a Navarr-held territory affected by the nation's decision.
t.Sarangrave: Trods must be placed in Béantal Dol in the Sarangrave before the final war can begin. Triggering its vallorn heart was argued to spell disaster for the occupying Druj.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the recent Druj invasion of Therunin is listed among the military difficulties facing the Empire.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Navarr scouts were to seek opportunities to place trods in Béantal Dol. Casting The Dance of Navarr and Thorn here is one of three castings needed to begin the final war, and they must be timed so the Druj cannot simply take them down.

The price of peace.d: The Thule treaty expires in Summer 387YE, and the Dragons will not talk until the Senate passes, word for word, a motion declaring Silver Peaks, Miechernya, Krevsaty, Crow's Ridge, Bonewood and Webwood part of Otkodov forever. Wintermark's hunt for Maarik the Golden Tongue drove her to Aino's Rest, and Ambassador Kindra Surefoot was made responsible for killing her. The Grendel, still at war, sent Speaker Morna to Anvil to discuss the Children of Wrecks. The Iron Confederacy warned it may aid the Grendel unless the Empire offers inducements. Skoura proposed a Treaty of Stone over Mareave and Tsark, and Lasambrian Jotun envoys arrived seeking Avisena, the Golden Jarl.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Consul Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn handles relations with Skoura and the Lasambrian Jotun, and negotiated the proposed Skouran treaty.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Imperial and Thule forces once fought side by side against the Druj in Ossium, a campaign in which the Thule took the Bonewood.
n.Grendel: The Grendel remain at war with the Empire but keep their embassy in Cargo open, and Speaker Morna was coming to Anvil to discuss cooperating against Shivaarn's Children of Wrecks, who have broken from them. The Iron Confederacy openly trades with them and was weighing material aid for them.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun delegation reached Highguard-held Casinea on its way to Anvil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skoura's proposed Treaty of Stone welcomed the Imperial Orcs to Mareave as 'scions of freedom' and fitting stewards of the lowlands once called Mahal. Crow's Ridge in their territory of Skarsind is among the regions the Thule demanded the Empire renounce.
n.Jotun: A delegation of Lasambrian Jotun, orcs sworn to the Jotun, crossed into the Empire under a flag of truce after their latest repulsed assault on Kahraman. They were due at Anvil to meet Avisena, the Golden Jarl, apparently on behalf of their own septs alone.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast citizens hold the embassies to the Grendel (Finna) and the Iron Confederacy (Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo), and former Segura senator Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra was named by the Lasambrian envoys as the person they wished to meet. Madruga remains contested by the Children of Wrecks.
n.Thule: The Dragons of Otkodov refused any talks on extending the peace until the Senate passes their exact motion recognising six ceded regions as Otkodov forever, after the earlier Senate wording enraged them. They signalled they expect a heavy price for further peace.
n.Varushka: The Thule used Wintermark's honouring of Yulia Kasimiova Voronov to publicly slight the Varushkans and called for a Wintermark ambassador instead. Varushkan-held regions Krevsaty, Miechernya, Bonewood and Webwood are among those the Thule demanded the Empire renounce.
n.Wintermark: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark became Ambassador to Otkodov, and nearly three thousand Wintermark heroes searched the Silver Peaks, forcing Maarik the Golden Tongue to retreat to Aino's Rest. Kindra is now responsible for killing her.

t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel threats make crossing the Bay treacherous, and the Children of Wrecks have claimed the entire Bay for their eternal. Skoura's proposed treaty would renounce all Skouran claims to territories on the Bay.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun delegation arrived in Casinea ahead of the Summer Solstice, heading to Anvil.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: a proposed Suranni-Imperial alliance to drive the Grendel from Feroz had collapsed because the Suranni expected to keep any regions they freed.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian Jotun had recently been driven back from their latest bloody assault on Kahraman before sending envoys to Anvil under a flag of truce.
t.Karsk: The Thule demanded that the Senate declare Krevsaty in Karsk, ceded in 379YE, part of Otkodov forever and renounce any claim to it.
t.Madruga: Madruga was assaulted by Grendel forces in Winter 385YE, and the passage to Free Landing is now impassable to armies, leaving it unclear how the Empire can defeat the Wreckers there.
t.Mareave: Skoura's proposed Treaty of Stone would acknowledge the Empire's conquest of Mareave, renounce Skoura's claim to it, welcome the Imperial Orcs, and ask the Empire to return Skouran artefacts uncovered there.
t.Miekarova: Miechernya in Miekarova, given to the Thule as payment for aid against the Jotun, is among the regions the Thule demanded the Empire recognise as Otkodov forever.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Skoura's proposed treaty would commit the Empire to consult Skoura on substantive matters concerning the Tsark of the Mountains of the Moon, with whom the Empire has no formal relations.
t.Ossium: Both the Bonewood, taken by the Thule while fighting the Druj, and the Webwood, ceded for aid against the Jotun, are named in the Thule's demand that the Empire renounce them forever.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov's Dragons set an exact Senate motion as their condition for opening talks to extend the peace that expires in Summer 387YE, and rejected an address by the Throne as a substitute.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's grasslands have seen a decade of Lasambrian invasion and retreat, and the envoys sought Avisena, once Segura's senator.
t.Sermersuaq: Wintermark armies hunted Maarik the Golden Tongue in Sermersuaq's Silver Peaks, driving her to her hideaway of Aino's Rest, where a skirmish to kill her is very likely to involve combat.
t.Skarsind: Crow's Ridge in Skarsind, taken by the Thule when the peace was extended in 382YE, is among the regions the Thule demanded the Empire renounce.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador operates from Chaubrette, a territory said to lie west of Veroigne.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The hills of Krevsaty, ceded in the 379YE treaty, must be declared part of Otkodov 'now and forever' in the Senate motion the Thule demand.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The passage to Free Landing has become impassable to armies, frustrating any short-term Imperial move against the Children of Wrecks.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Miechernya, the Thule's price for aid against the Jotun, is named in the motion the Dragons insist the Senate pass before any talks.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Bonewood, conquered by the Thule while fighting the Druj, was left out of the Senate's earlier motion but is named in the exact wording the Dragons now demand.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Webwood, ceded for Thule aid against the Jotun, is among the regions the Empire is asked to renounce forever.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: With Thule permission, Wintermark forces searched the Silver Peaks for Maarik the Golden Tongue, who has withdrawn to Aino's Rest. The region is also named in the Thule's demand for permanent recognition as Otkodov.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Ridge, taken by the Thule when the peace was extended in 382YE, is named in the motion the Dragons insist the Senate pass unchanged.

The way home.d: Eilian Sweetwater's proposal let the Navarr commission a wayhouse sinecure in any non-Navarr Imperial territory with a trod network, outside City regions, with a Navarr keeper. The first wayhouse in a territory would raise Imperial taxation there by eight crowns, and Navarr living nearby would avoid the foreign-nation penalty and share in local great works, though they could not vote for that territory's senator. Three projects were offered: restoring Myfanwy's Rest in Fishguard, Necropolis; the Last Battle Striding's wayhouse beside an enemy territory holding a vallorn heart, which would put that territory's regions under threat; and the Scale and the Source's Primal Forest for sharing magical traditions. The Myfanwy's Rest and Primal Forest opportunities later expired.

n.Dawn: The Plains of Teeth in the Dawnish-held Barrens was named as a possible site for the Last Battle wayhouse, from which Navarr thorns would scout into the Sarangrave.
n.Druj: A Last Battle wayhouse built next to the Druj-held Sarangrave would let Navarr thorns patrol across the border and put the Sarangrave's regions under threat.
n.Highguard: Restoring Myfanwy's Rest in Necropolis promised a steady stream of Highborn visitors, with Navarr historians meeting Highborn archivists, benefactors, grey pilgrims and wayfarers to study the founding of the Empire.
n.Jotun: Liathaven, held by the Jotun and containing a vallorn heart, was named as a territory whose regions would come under threat if the Last Battle wayhouse were built in the neighbouring Grey Fens.
n.Navarr: Navarr gained the means to build wayhouse sinecures with Navarr keepers in other nations' territories, at the price of their residents losing a vote for a senator, and three striding and wayhouse projects sought the nation's support.
n.The Marches: The Grey Fens in Bregasland was named as a possible site for the Last Battle wayhouse, and any wayhouse built in a Marcher territory would raise its Imperial taxation and bring Navarr settlers.
n.Thule: The Scale and the Source suggested the Primal Forest could forge links with the warlocks of Thule-held Otkodov and discuss the vallorn in Sküld.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen was called the obvious choice of nation for the Primal Forest's exchange of magical learning.
n.Varushka: The Primal Forest was pitched as a way to bond Varushkan cabalists with Navarr vates, noting that Varushka borders Sküld.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland's Grey Fens was offered as an example site for the Last Battle wayhouse, as it borders vallorn-infested Liathaven.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Navarr living in Brocéliande were noted as unable to vote for a senator but still hopeful that one day they might.
t.Liathaven: As an enemy-held territory with a vallorn heart, Liathaven's uncontrolled regions would come under threat if Navarr thorns built a Last Battle wayhouse in the Grey Fens.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis was home to Myfanwy's Rest, the Empire's most famous wayhouse, which Eirian asked the Navarr to restore with a library and a collection of founding-era relics.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov's warlocks and the vallorn in Sküld were cited as reasons a Varushkan-linked Primal Forest wayhouse could prove valuable.
t.Sarangrave: The Sarangrave was named as an enemy territory with a vallorn heart whose regions a Last Battle wayhouse on the Plains of Teeth would put under threat.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens' Plains of Teeth was suggested as a site for the Last Battle wayhouse, giving Navarr thorns a base for patrols into the Sarangrave.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Navarr in Therunin were noted alongside those in Liathaven and Brocéliande as being unable to vote for a senator.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Grey Fens was proposed as a home for the Last Battle wayhouse, where Navarr thorns would scout across the border into Liathaven.
r.Necropolis/Fishguard: Fishguard held Myfanwy's Rest, legendary home of the First Empress's companion Myfanwy, and was the site of the proposed restoration with a Navarr Keeper drawing liao and crowns.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Sküld was cited as a place on Varushka's borders where the vallorn could be discussed with the warlocks of Otkodov through the Primal Forest.

Thrones and principalities.d: Relations with Jarm remained hostile after the Liberty Pact, the sharing of Imperial lore with the Commonwealth and the Senate's embargo, and Jarm was at open war with the Commonwealth. Jarm had founded the Freedom Accord with Asavea and the Sarcophan Delves. Ambassador Anton Trescher offered the shield Measure in exchange for the Conclave disseminating Brotherhood of Tian. Jarm would add 10 rings of ilium for the disseminating order and 100 thrones to the Senate as clear inducements. Bojana Etura of the Circle of Six offered to buy ritual items in bulk through Guildmaster Xanthius, with collection planned at the Autumn Equinox. Trescher curtly dismissed warnings about the Hand of Dumon.

n.Grendel: Jarm had earlier supplied the Grendel with magical aid, including fortification rituals and rumoured mana, vis and foci, until Prospero's intervention ended it. The two still trade openly, and the Grendel are rumoured to have been approached to join the Freedom Accord, possibly already as signatories.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the new Imperial ambassador to Jarm, Nikita Teanga Volkov, is of Varushka and had worked to reopen communication with the Jarmish.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Ambassador Trescher cited the situation in the Bay of Catazar as a reason the Empire might struggle to convey the shield from Jarm.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is named among the ports the House of Princes refuses to let Imperial fleets visit, apparently a variant spelling of the Jarmish port Kavor.

Towers and crows.d: Relations with the Delves stayed positive but were tinged with disappointment after several failed trade deals, and the Delves remained determined to stay neutral in the wars. They proposed opening negotiations at two thrones a wain for mithril, weirwood or white granite, or three thrones for weirwood if they could sell it straight on to the Grendel. The civil service noted that the legality of this was murky. The Sarcophan were troubled by Conclave-endorsed storm magic and resented the unwarned storms on their Sarvos enclave. Fearing for their neutrality, they offered 18 thrones for the Regario Dossier rather than an exchange of intelligence. They also declined to share anything about the Elakar or the Book of Silence.

n.Grendel: The Grendel were the unnamed 'local buyer' already buying all the weirwood the Delves could supply to build navies. Any Imperial weirwood sold through the Sarcophan would speed their shipbuilding.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan were not trading much in Madruga anyway because of the turmoil in that Brass Coast territory.
n.The League: The Sarcophan enclave in the old Alivetti estates in Sarvos was hit by storms before the Spring Equinox. The Vandersaar family were aggrieved that they had not been warned and that no apology followed.
n.Wintermark: Thanmir Hrafnar of Wintermark, the Imperial ambassador to the Delves, gave no apology for the Sarvos storms, which irked the Vandersaar. The Sarcophan did thank him for his candid advice on their narcotic herb proposals and intended to follow it.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay had become a war zone and its piracy risk depressed the price the Sarcophan would pay for bourse materials. They proposed carrying weirwood safely across it to the Grendel, and they were wary of the recent storm magic cast on its waters.
t.Madruga: Madruga was the only place where the warned-of storms actually materialised. The Sarcophan were not trading much there anyway because of the turmoil in the territory.
t.Sarvos: Storms before the Spring Equinox struck the Vandersaar family's Alivetti estates, ceded to the Delves in 383YE. Local Sarcophan were angry that they had received no warning.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: named as an alternative shipping route for bourse materials that was no safer than the Bay of Catazar.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: reaching the Semmerlak through the Mallum was named as an alternative shipping route that was no safer than the Bay.

Tread of dust and darkness.d: Gideon of the Farthest Shore concluded that the Blight's power was gathering at the abandoned di Tutamen villa, probably in the missing body of Aldea di Tutamen, which sits in a Winter regio. A five-person conjunction to the villa was identified and assigned to the Hakima of Salt and Sand. Aligning the regio with Spring might let the Rainmaker Ossegrahn claim it and cut the Blight off. That would make it safer to cast Dyan of Eagle's Striding's projection, held by Grandmaster Eliza, which would flood the Scorrero and wash the region clean. Separately, Azoth studied Dry Patrician ashes for Bakar i Riqueza. Detachments of the Drakes and the Burning Falcon had also corralled two groups of displaced Parched.

n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast figures stood at the centre of the struggle. The Hakima of Salt and Sand was charged with the conjunction to the Blight's heart, Bakar i Riqueza awaited Azoth's alchemical research, and General Aracelis i Erigo had to defeat Parched cornered by the Burning Falcon's kohan to return 50 strength to the army.

t.Madruga: The Blight still holds the ashen desert of Blightheart, though its power has drawn inward to the di Tutamen villa. Proposed remedies include claiming its regio through Ossegrahn and flooding the land via the Scorrero, while Imperial armies hold off stray Parched displaced by the storms.
t.Segura: Ashes from the Dry Patrician that attacked Segura were delivered to Azoth. The Crucible's study of them may yield a new ritual alchemy for Bakar i Riqueza once the Blight is resolved.

r.Segura/Lucksprings: The hard-fought Spring Equinox incursion against the Parched in Lucksprings is where Bakar i Riqueza apparently claimed the Dry Patrician dust and ashes that Azoth is now studying.

Who goes there?.d: Kay de Revoile planned to open a magical pouch in the Dawnish Glory Square. Endric of Lepidus sought musical settings of Elayne Silverlark's lyrics at the Navarr Song and Story Circle. Hahnmark's revived Strengths of the Deeps coven wanted advice from herb-garden owners on whether to use a Winter boon from the Hungry Wolf. Ale di Sarvos offered a strange tombola with prizes including White Granite. Lost Lore Steading urged that Navarr priests advise and scrutinise vates. Mystics of the Aviary of Ishal sought fellow mystics at the Tree of Names. The herald Archipelago asked Jackdaw Larksong to lead a team inside him to cure his indigestion.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: several members of the Strengths of the Deeps coven died in what they called a badly mishandled battle against the Druj, after which the coven stopped coming to Anvil.
n.Navarr: Lost Lore Steading called on the Navarr to scrutinise their vates more closely, urging priests to advise vates on their oaths and on dealings with eternals, though the idea met a mixed reception. Endric of Lepidus also planned to visit the Song and Story Circle in the Navarr camp to hear new settings of Silverlark's lyrics.
n.Wintermark: The Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp was chosen as a meeting place by the Hahnmark coven weighing a Winter boon, by mystics of the Aviary of Ishal discussing the future role of mystics, and by the tombola-running mountebanks.

t.Hahnmark: The Strengths of the Deeps coven had returned to their old hall at Gulnar's Deeps and begun clearing a neglected Winter regio. They held a boon from the Hungry Wolf that might benefit all Hahnmark, and sought counsel from the territory's herb-garden owners before deciding whether to use it.
t.Miaren: Lost Lore Steading in Miaren, known for valuing Vigilance and Wisdom, sent out a call for priests to advise the vates. Its artisans made eye-and-thorn tokens to mark the priests who take on that role.

Winds and flames.d: The Liege Tchinua Ganbatar has favoured closer ties with the Empire since a coup in 384YE, and Mistress Singua Karadragha now serves as ambassador. High Lady Togene Altsanig opposes the Empire and appears to have Asavean allies. Many Faraden blame the Marches for the razing of Moonwater Hall. The Empire could commission a new Faraden trade enclave as a great work, costing 20 white granite, 20 weirwood and 120 crowns, which would raise business investment in the chosen territory by one. Several trade offers were also on the table: Faraden interest in weirwood at about two thrones a wain, an offer of 50 thrones for 25 wains from Pelabuhan, and a request for up to 150 iridescent gloaming from the Blue Silken Scarf guild.

n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun of Reinos heavily tax Faraden caravans, and Faraden would welcome an Imperial attack or conquest of Reinos to open a direct land route and secure its own border.
n.The Brass Coast: A new Faraden trade enclave could be built anywhere in the Brass Coast, raising business investment there. Any boost to trade from a conquered Reinos would likely also raise taxation in the south-west.
n.The League: Tassato is one of the territories where a replacement Faraden trade enclave could be built, raising business investment there.
n.The Marches: Many Faraden blame the Marches for the destruction of Moonwater Hall, and a Marcher ambassador, Ebenezer, has drawn suspicion. Mournwold, Mitwold and Upwold are candidate sites for a new enclave.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark and Kallavesa are candidate sites for a new Faraden trade enclave, though building in marshy Kallavesa may cost more labour.

t.Hahnmark: A replacement Faraden trade enclave could be built here, raising business investment in the territory by one.
t.Kahraman: As Brass Coast land, Kahraman could host a new Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa could host the new Faraden enclave, though its marshy terrain may increase the labour cost.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold is a possible site for a replacement Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold is a possible site for a new Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.
t.Reinos: The Jotun tax Faraden caravans through Reinos, and Faraden would welcome an Imperial expeditionary force or conquest here. Conquest would open a direct land trade route to the Empire.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: it is described as the dangerous sea route that few Faraden attempt, and which a land route through Reinos would avoid.
t.Segura: As Brass Coast land, Segura could host a new Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.
t.Tassato: Tassato is a possible site for a replacement Faraden trade enclave that would raise business investment by one.
t.Upwold: Upwold was home to the original Moonwater Hall and is again a possible site for a new Faraden trade enclave.

r.Upwold/Tower March: The original Moonwater Hall stood near King's Stoke in Tower March until the Senate had it torn down in Spring 384YE, an act many Faraden still resent.
